docs.title: Methods you call on a fit
docs.text:
These work on a fitted model the same way as in metafor. The result object is passed as the first argument.

res = rma('yi', 'vi', mods='~ ablat', data=dat)

docs.title: predict
docs.text:
from metafopy import predict

print(predict(res, newmods=[10, 30, 50]))
print(predict(rma('yi', 'vi', data=dat), transf=numpy.exp))

     pred      se   ci.lb   ci.ub   pi.lb   pi.ub
0 -0.0396  0.1866 -0.4053  0.3262 -0.6931  0.6140
1 -0.6216  0.1069 -0.8312 -0.4120 -1.2023 -0.0409
2 -1.2036  0.1716 -1.5400 -0.8672 -1.8412 -0.5660
     pred   ci.lb   ci.ub   pi.lb  pi.ub
0  0.4894  0.3441  0.6962  0.1546  1.549

transf= applies a transformation to the predictions and their bounds. Prediction intervals (pi.lb, pi.ub) include the heterogeneity. predtype= (pi_type= is its old spelling) chooses how the interval is built: 'default', 'simple' (no uncertainty of the predicted value, normal distribution), 'riley' (a t distribution with k - parms degrees of freedom, Riley et al., 2011, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-985X.2010.00696.x) or 't'; newvi= adds the sampling variances of new studies. Both work for every fit class. na_action= ('omit', 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail', standing for R's options(na.action=)) decides whether the fitted values of fitted(), predict() and hatvalues() cover the studies used in fitting or one value for each study of the data.

newmods= may also be a pandas.Series, a dict or a one- or multi-row pandas.DataFrame with names. With more than one moderator the values are then matched to the moderators by name, in any order and also by partial names (a name is accepted when its letters occur in order in the moderator's name and only one moderator fits, so {'yr': 1960, 'abl': 30} matches year and ablat), as in R. prob='>log(0.8)' evaluates the cutoff (arithmetic and common functions such as log, exp and sqrt), and addx=True adds the model matrix as columns X.intrcpt, X.ablat, ... to the printed result and to to_frame().

docs.title: confint
docs.text:
For a random-effects model, confint gives intervals for tau^2, tau, I^2 and H^2. The default is the Q-profile method of Viechtbauer (2007), https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.2514. type='pl' gives profile-likelihood intervals.

from metafopy import confint

print(confint(res))
print(confint(res, type='pl'))

        estimate    ci.lb    ci.ub
tau^2     0.0764   0.0167   0.7849
tau       0.2763   0.1292   0.8859
I^2(%)   68.3931  32.1080  95.6976
H^2       3.1639   1.4729  23.2428
        estimate    ci.lb    ci.ub
tau^2     0.0764   0.0058   0.4432
tau       0.2763   0.0763   0.6657
I^2(%)   68.3931  14.1564  92.6258
H^2       3.1639   1.1649  13.5607

docs.title: anova
docs.text:
anova runs Wald-type tests of coefficients and likelihood ratio tests that compare two nested models. Fit both with method='ML' for the likelihood ratio test of fixed effects.

from metafopy import anova

full = rma('yi', 'vi', mods='~ ablat', data=dat, method='ML')
reduced = rma('yi', 'vi', data=dat, method='ML')
print(anova(full, reduced))
print(anova(res, btt=[1]))

         df      AIC      BIC     AICc   logLik     LRT    pval        QE   tau^2      R^2
Full      3  21.3713  23.0662  24.0380  -7.6857     NaN     NaN   30.7331  0.0344      NaN
Reduced   2  29.3302  30.4601  30.5302 -12.6651  9.9588  0.0016  152.2330  0.2800  87.7302
Test of Moderators (coefficient 2):
QM(df = 1) = 16.3571, p-val < .0001

For a fit made robust with robust(res, cluster, club_sandwich=True), anova runs the cluster-robust Wald test with the small-sample approximation of the fit's wald_test (HTZ by default), which gives an F test with an estimated denominator degrees of freedom (F(df1 = 1, df2 = 1.52) = 41.6109, p-val = 0.0440 for btt on the bcg data with cluster='alloc'); anova(res, X=...) uses the degrees of freedom of the fit's coef_test for each linear combination. L is R's old spelling of X, fixed=True matches a character btt literally, and anova(full, reduced, test='Wald') tests the extra coefficients of the full model with its Wald test.

docs.title: Permutation test
docs.text:
permutest gives permutation-based p-values for the coefficients, with an exact test for small numbers of studies. Set the seed with set_seed first: metafopy reproduces R's random number generator, so seeds give the same permutations as set.seed in R.

from metafopy import permutest, set_seed

set_seed(1234)
print(permutest(res, iter=500))

Test of Moderators (coefficient 2):¹
QM(df = 1) = 16.3571, p-val = 0.0100

Model Results:

         estimate      se     zval    pval¹    ci.lb    ci.ub
intrcpt    0.2515  0.2491   1.0095  0.6980   -0.2368   0.7397
ablat     -0.0291  0.0072  -4.0444  0.0100   -0.0432  -0.0150  **

---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

1) p-values based on permutation testing

docs.title: profile
docs.text:
profile evaluates the likelihood over a grid of tau^2 values, which is useful to see whether the likelihood is flat:

from metafopy import profile

print(profile(rma('yi', 'vi', data=dat)).tau2[:3])

[0.11969531 0.17189484 0.22409436]

profile(..., pred=True, newmods=...) adds the predicted values and their interval bounds at each grid value (pred, pred_ci_lb, pred_ci_ub, pred_pi_lb, pred_pi_ub) and blup=True the BLUPs (blup, blup_se, blup_pi_lb, blup_pi_ub) to the result.

docs.title: Residuals and BLUPs
docs.text: rstandard, rstudent, blup and ranef give residuals and the best linear unbiased predictions of the study-specific effects. See Diagnostics.

docs.title: Equal-effects and fixed-effects models
docs.text: method='EE' fits the equal-effects model: every study estimates the same true effect. metafor also accepts 'FE' and 'CE' as synonyms. The results are identical and only the interpretation differs. A random-effects model estimates the mean of a distribution of true effects instead. See Hedges and Vevea (1998), https://doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.3.4.486, for the distinction.

docs.title: Weights
docs.text: weights replaces the inverse-variance weights with your own, and weighted=False fits by ordinary least squares. The standard errors of the coefficients then account for the weights not being inverse-variance weights. For inference that is robust to a misspecified model, see robust.

docs.title: Multilevel and multivariate models
docs.text:
rma_mv fits models in which the effect sizes are not independent: several effect sizes per study, studies nested in districts, several outcomes measured in the same subjects, effects that share a sampling error or are correlated through a phylogeny. It mirrors metafor's rma.mv and follows the interface closely:

  • yi: the effect sizes, and V: their sampling variances or the whole variance-covariance matrix.
  • random: one or more formulas of the form ~ 1 | factor (random intercepts) or ~ inner | outer (a structured variance-covariance matrix). Nested factors are written ~ 1 | district/school.
  • struct: the structure of the variance-covariance matrix for ~ inner | outer terms.

docs.title: A three-level model
docs.text:
The schools data of Konstantopoulos (2011), https://doi.org/10.1002/jrsm.35, have studies (schools) nested in districts:

from metafopy import datasets, rma_mv

dat = datasets.load('dat.konstantopoulos2011')
res = rma_mv(yi='yi', V='vi', random='~ 1 | district/school', data=dat)
print(res)

Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 56; method: REML)

Variance Components:

            estim    sqrt  nlvls  fixed           factor
sigma^2.1  0.0651  0.2551     11     no         district
sigma^2.2  0.0327  0.1809     56     no  district/school

Test for Heterogeneity:
Q(df = 55) = 578.8640, p-val < .0001

Model Results:

estimate      se    zval    pval   ci.lb   ci.ub
  0.1847  0.0846  2.1845  0.0289  0.0190  0.3504  *

---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

The variance components are sigma^2.1 (between districts) and sigma^2.2 (between schools within districts).

docs.title: Several effect sizes per study
docs.text:
When a study contributes several effect sizes, the sampling errors are correlated. If the correlation is unknown, assume one and build the sampling variance-covariance matrix with vcalc, then check the sensitivity of the conclusions to it:

from metafopy import vcalc

dat = datasets.load('dat.assink2016')
V = vcalc(vi=dat['vi'], cluster=dat['study'], obs=dat['esid'], rho=0.6)
res = rma_mv(yi='yi', V=V, random='~ 1 | study/esid', data=dat)
print(res)

Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 100; method: REML)

Variance Components:

            estim    sqrt  nlvls  fixed      factor
sigma^2.1  0.0807  0.2841     17     no       study
sigma^2.2  0.1545  0.3931    100     no  study/esid

Test for Heterogeneity:
Q(df = 99) = 745.4385, p-val < .0001

Model Results:

estimate      se    zval    pval   ci.lb   ci.ub
  0.3678  0.0965  3.8097  0.0001  0.1786  0.5570  ***

---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

rcalc does the same for correlation coefficients, and bldiag and blsplit build and split block-diagonal matrices.

docs.title: Moderators
docs.text:
Moderators work as in rma_uni, with mods:

res = rma_mv(yi='yi', V=V, mods='~ year', random='~ 1 | study/esid', data=dat)
print(res)

Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 100; method: REML)

Variance Components:

            estim    sqrt  nlvls  fixed      factor
sigma^2.1  0.0408  0.2019     17     no       study
sigma^2.2  0.1557  0.3945    100     no  study/esid

Test for Residual Heterogeneity:
QE(df = 98) = 743.4621, p-val < .0001

Test of Moderators (coefficient 2):

docs.title: Cluster-robust inference
docs.text:
If the dependence structure is only approximately right, use cluster-robust (sandwich) inference. robust replaces the standard errors, tests and confidence intervals of a fit, with the study as the cluster (Hedges et al., 2010, https://doi.org/10.1002/jrsm.5):

from metafopy import robust

print(robust(res, cluster=dat['study']))

Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 100; method: REML)

Variance Components:

            estim    sqrt  nlvls  fixed      factor
sigma^2.1  0.0408  0.2019     17     no       study
sigma^2.2  0.1557  0.3945    100     no  study/esid

Test for Residual Heterogeneity:
QE(df = 98) = 743.4621, p-val < .0001

Number of estimates:   100
Number of clusters:    17
Estimates per cluster: 1-22 (mean: 5.88, median: 5)

Test of Moderators (coefficient 2):¹
F(df1 = 1, df2 = 15) = 3.2611, p-val = 0.0910

Model Results:

         estimate      se¹     tval¹  df¹    pval¹    ci.lb¹   ci.ub¹
intrcpt    0.3835  0.0912    4.2059   15   0.0008    0.1892   0.5779   ***
year      -0.0388  0.0215   -1.8058   15   0.0910   -0.0845   0.0070     .

---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

1) results based on cluster-robust inference (var-cov estimator: CR1,
   approx t/F-tests and confidence intervals, df: residual method)

The default is metafor's CR1 estimator with a t-test. club_sandwich=True uses the CR0 to CR3 estimators with the small-sample corrections of the R package clubSandwich; see Pustejovsky and Tipton (2018), https://doi.org/10.1080/07350015.2016.1247004.

docs.title: Confidence intervals for variance components
docs.text:
from metafopy import confint

print(confint(rma_mv(yi='yi', V='vi', random='~ 1 | study/esid', data=dat), sigma2=1))

           estimate   ci.lb   ci.ub
sigma^2.2    0.1120  0.0671  0.1810
sigma.2      0.3347  0.2590  0.4255

The profile-likelihood interval for the component with 0-based index sigma2=1 is computed. Without an index, intervals for all components are returned.

docs.title: Optimiser and Hessian settings
docs.text: control= of rma_mv takes the arguments of metafor: optimizer ('nlminb' by default, here BFGS with the analytic score; 'optim' with optmethod, 'nlm', 'bobyqa', 'hjk' and the others of rma.mv are run on the log-likelihood alone, optim's BFGS and Nelder-Mead as exact ports and the rest with the closest SciPy method), ncpus, parallel and cl (accepted, but the likelihood is always evaluated serially), mfmaxit (the number of likelihood evaluations after which the fit stops with an error), nearpd (force the G, H and M matrices to be positive definite, which the cvvc example of ?matreg needs to obtain res.vvc) and hesspack ('numDeriv', 'pracma' or 'calculus') with hessianCtrl for the Hessians of optbeta and cvvc.

docs.title: Known correlation matrices
docs.text:
For phylogenetic and other known structures, give the correlation matrix as R={'species.id': matrix}: a dict of DataFrames whose row and column names match the levels of the grouping factor. The bundled dat.moura2021 comes with its phylogenetic tree (Moura et al., 2021), and PhyloTree.vcv turns the tree into a correlation matrix, as ape::vcv does in R. This model has many effect sizes and takes a while to fit:

# docs: skip
tree = datasets.load_tree('dat.moura2021.tree')
dat = escalc(measure='ZCOR', ri='ri', ni='ni', data=datasets.load('dat.moura2021'))
dat['obs'] = range(1, len(dat) + 1)
res = rma_mv(yi='yi', V='vi', random=['~ 1 | species.id', '~ 1 | study.id', '~ 1 | obs'], R={'species.id': tree.vcv(corr=True)}, data=dat)
print(res)

See the R argument of rma_mv.

docs.title: What works on an rma_mv fit
docs.text:
predict, anova, confint (profile-likelihood intervals for the variance components), profile, ranef, robust, cooks_distance, dfbetas, rstandard and rstudent accept an rma_mv fit, as does its hatvalues() method. The case-deletion diagnostics refit the model without each observation, or without each cluster given as cluster=:

from metafopy import cooks_distance, ranef, rstudent

dat = datasets.load('dat.konstantopoulos2011')
res = rma_mv(yi='yi', V='vi', random='~ 1 | district/school', data=dat)
print(cooks_distance(res, cluster='district'))
print(rstudent(res, cluster='district'))
print(ranef(res)['district'])

As in metafor, influence, leave1out and qqnorm are not available for rma_mv fits, see Diagnostics.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
metafopy draws plots with matplotlib. Each plot function draws on the current axes (or on an axes object passed as ax=) and returns a result object that holds what was plotted. Save and show figures with the usual matplotlib functions.

The plot gallery reproduces the plots of the metafor documentation with metafopy, and compares them with the R figures.

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use('Agg')

import matplotlib.pyplot
import numpy

from metafopy import datasets, escalc, rma

dat = escalc(measure='RR', ai='tpos', bi='tneg', ci='cpos', di='cneg', data=datasets.load('dat.bcg'))
dat['label'] = dat['author'] + ', ' + dat['year'].astype(str)
res = rma('yi', 'vi', data=dat, slab=dat['label'])

docs.title: Forest plot
docs.text:
from metafopy import forest

forest(res, atransf=numpy.exp, header=True)
matplotlib.pyplot.savefig('forest.png', dpi=150)

atransf transforms the axis labels (here to risk ratios) while the plot stays on the log scale, and transf transforms the estimates themselves. Other common arguments are:

  • order: 'obs' sorts by effect size, 'prec' by precision, or give your own values.
  • ilab, ilab_lab, ilab_xpos: columns of study information shown next to the plot.
  • addpred=True: add the prediction interval to the summary.
  • showweights=True: show the weights.
  • xlim, alim, at, refline, xlab, digits, slab.
  • na_action='pass': keep the studies dropped for missing values as (empty) rows of the plot, as metafor does under options(na.action='na.pass').

For plots with subgroups, draw the studies with forest(..., rows=...) and the summaries with addpoly. Examples are in the metafor documentation: https://www.metafor-project.org/doku.php/plots:forest_plot_with_subgroups. The gallery also reproduces the BMJ, RevMan and superscript styles.

from metafopy import forest

forest(res, atransf=numpy.exp, order='obs', addpred=True, xlab='Risk ratio')
matplotlib.pyplot.savefig('forest-sorted.png')

docs.title: Funnel plot
docs.text:
from metafopy import funnel

matplotlib.pyplot.figure()
funnel(res)
matplotlib.pyplot.savefig('funnel.png')

yaxis sets the vertical axis ('sei' is the default, also 'vi', 'seinv', 'vinv', 'ni', 'ninv', 'sqrtni', 'sqrtninv', 'lni', 'wi'), level and shade draw the contours of statistical significance (contour-enhanced funnel plots, Peters et al., 2008, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclinepi.2007.11.010), and funnel(trimfill(res)) shows the filled studies.

matplotlib.pyplot.figure()
funnel(res, level=[90, 95, 99], shade=['white', 'gray55', 'gray75'], refline=0)
matplotlib.pyplot.savefig('funnel-contours.png')

docs.title: Other plots
docs.text:
Function Plot radial Radial (Galbraith) plot labbe L'Abbe plot of 2x2 table event rates baujat Baujat plot, which studies drive the heterogeneity qqnorm Normal quantile-quantile plot of the residuals, with a simulated envelope plot_infl Case deletion diagnostics, see Diagnostics plot_profile Profile likelihood of a variance component, from profile; given the list profile returns for rma_mv, location-scale and selection models it draws one panel per component plot_gosh GOSH plot regplot, points_regplot Meta-analytic scatterplot of a model with one moderator (rma_uni, location-scale, selmodel, rma_mv and rma_glmm fits), with the regression line, confidence band and sized points; points_regplot redraws the points and labels of the result forest_cumul, plot_cumul Forest plot and plot of the results of a cumul analysis (forest(cumul(res)) calls the first) llplot Log-likelihoods of the studies as a function of the effect (OR or generic) plot_permutest Permutation distributions of a permutest result plot_vif Simulated (G)VIFs of a vif(sim=True) result plot_selmodel Selection function of a selmodel fit 
from metafopy import baujat, qqnorm, radial

matplotlib.pyplot.figure()
radial(res)
matplotlib.pyplot.figure()
baujat(res)
matplotlib.pyplot.figure()
qqnorm(res)

The gallery has more examples of each plot, and the plot of the influence diagnostics, the GOSH plot and the L'Abbe plot.

docs.title: Styling
docs.text: Fonts and sizes are matplotlib's. fonts takes the family names metafor uses ('sans', 'serif', 'mono'), and cex, cex_lab, cex_axis scale the text as in R. For anything else, pass your own ax= and use matplotlib on it.

docs.title: metafopy showcase¶
docs.text:
This notebook shows what meta-analysis looks like when it lives in Python and Jupyter. Every number comes from metafopy; the charts are Altair (Vega-Lite) charts that stay interactive on the static docs site, because the fits are computed here in Python and the browser only filters them. The statistics are those of the R package metafor (Viechtbauer, 2010, doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03); the plots are free to look different, see Plots compared with metafor for the matplotlib versions that mirror R.

The story: a main thread on the BCG vaccine trials (Colditz et al., 1994, doi:10.1001/jama.1994.03520050036011), then two side trips: a multilevel model for schools nested in districts (Konstantopoulos, 2011, doi:10.1002/jrsm.35) and publication bias in passive smoking and lung cancer (Hackshaw et al., 1997, doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7114.980), and a generated write-up with exported figures.

Hover for tooltips, click a study to highlight it everywhere, drag in the funnel plot to brush, and use the controls above the forest plot.

docs.title: 1. The data and a first model¶
docs.text: escalc turns the 2x2 tables of the 13 trials into log risk ratios and sampling variances; rma fits the random-effects model. Results render as tables here (the printed text of R's summary() is still what print(fit) gives).

docs.title: 2. Everything a study contributes, in one frame¶
docs.text: The charts below share one tidy frame with a row per study: effect and interval, weight, the coordinates of the funnel and Baujat plots, and the influence diagnostics of influence().

docs.title: 3. Fit every estimator, with and without each trial¶
docs.text: The pooled estimate depends on two choices: which estimator of the between-trial variance tau^2 you use (metafopy has seven, see Veroniki et al. (2016)), and whether you leave one trial out to see if it drives the result. Here every combination is fitted once, in Python: 7 estimators x 14 options (leave out none, or one of the 13 trials) = 98 fits. Each row of the pooled frame is one fit, with its pooled risk ratio, intervals, tau^2 and I^2. The next cell prints the range of the pooled risk ratio (est) and of tau^2 over the 14 options for each estimator; section 4 turns the same frame into controls.

docs.title: 4. Linked forest, funnel, Baujat and meta-regression plots¶
docs.text: Click a study (shift-click for several) or brush a region of the funnel plot: the same studies light up in all four plots. The radio buttons and the "Leave out" drop-down below the charts pick a row of the pooled frame of section 3, the tau^2 estimator and the omitted trial; the red line and band in the forest plot, and the numbers above it, follow. The bubble plot is the meta-regression on absolute latitude, the moderator that explains most of the heterogeneity (predict(..., newmods=) draws the band).

docs.title: 5. Cumulative meta-analysis¶
docs.text: cumul() adds the trials one at a time in the order you give, here by publication year. The chart lets you change the estimator and shows how the estimate settles as the evidence accumulates.

docs.title: 6. GOSH: all subsets of the studies¶
docs.text: Olkin, Dahabreh and Trikalinos (2012) fit the model to every possible subset of studies (here 2^13 - 1 = 8191 fits) and plot the pooled estimate against I^2. Clusters point at a subgroup of studies that behave differently. Brush a region of the scatterplot: the histogram shows the estimates in the brush, and the bars show how often each trial is in those subsets.

docs.title: Side trip: schools nested in districts¶
docs.text: dat.konstantopoulos2011 has 56 studies of the effect of modified school calendars on achievement, from 11 districts. Studies in one district are not independent, so rma_mv adds a random effect for district and one for school within district (Konstantopoulos, 2011).

docs.title: Side trip: publication bias¶
docs.text: dat.hackshaw1998 pools 37 studies of lung cancer risk and passive smoking. The funnel plot below marks the studies that the trim-and-fill method (Duval and Tweedie, 2000, doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2000.00455.x) would add to make it symmetric; hover them to see how much each would change the picture.

docs.title: A generated write-up¶
docs.text: metafor's reporter() writes a report of a fit; metafopy does not port it, because a notebook does the job better: the text below is built from the fits above, so it cannot disagree with them.

docs.title: Results¶
docs.text:
We pooled 13 randomised trials of BCG vaccination with a random-effects model (REML estimate of τ²). The pooled risk ratio of tuberculosis was 0.49 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.70; 95% prediction interval 0.15 to 1.55). The trials were heterogeneous (Q(12) = 152.2, p < .0001; τ² = 0.313; I² = 92.2%).

Absolute latitude explained a large part of the heterogeneity: each additional degree of latitude changed the log risk ratio by -0.029 (95% CI -0.043 to -0.015; QM(1) = 16.4), with R² = 75.6%.

Across the 7 τ² estimators the pooled risk ratio ranged from 0.488 to 0.491.

docs.title: Exported figures¶
docs.text: The same fits drive static figures for a paper: the matplotlib forest plot of metafopy, and the Altair charts saved as SVG or PNG with vl-convert (no browser needed). The files go to a temporary directory; point out anywhere you like.

docs.title: Where next¶
docs.text:
• User guide and function reference for everything not shown here.
  • Coming from R if you know metafor already.
  • Run this notebook yourself: pip install "metafopy[interactive]" jupyterlab, or use the Binder badge at the top.

docs.title: Function reference
docs.text:
Generated from the docstrings, which link to the matching metafor documentation. Arguments follow metafor, with . replaced by _, so the metafor reference describes them in more detail.

  • Effect sizes: escalc and helpers.
  • Models: rma_uni, rma_mh, rma_peto, rma_glmm, rma_mv, selmodel, and the result classes.
  • Methods for fitted models: predict, confint, anova, diagnostics and the variance-covariance helpers.
  • Publication bias: regtest, ranktest, trimfill, fsn, hc, tes.
  • Plots: forest, funnel and the other plots.
  • Transformations: the transf_* functions.
  • Datasets: datasets.load and friends.
  • Errors: the exceptions metafopy raises.

docs.text: Tests and methods for publication bias and small-study effects, see Publication bias.

docs.title: regtest
docs.text:
Regression test for funnel plot asymmetry (metafor's regtest).

Sterne & Egger (2005), doi:10.1002/0470870168.ch6 -- the test adds the standard error (or another measure of precision) as a predictor to the meta-analytic model. See https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/regtest.html.

regtest(
    x: RMAResult | FixedBinaryResult | ArrayLike | str,
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    *,
    sei: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    ni: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | None = None,
    data: DataFrame | None = None,
    model: Literal['lm', 'rma'] = 'rma',
    predictor: Literal[
        'sei', 'vi', 'ni', 'ninv', 'sqrtni', 'sqrtninv'
    ] = 'sei',
    ret_fit: bool = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    method: str | None = None,
    test: str | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> RegtestResult

Regression test for funnel plot asymmetry (Egger's test and extensions).

Mirrors metafor's regtest. The effect sizes are regressed on a measure of their precision (the standard error by default) and the test for the coefficient of that predictor is the test for asymmetry (Egger et al., 1997, doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7109.629). With a fitted model that has moderators, the predictor is added to the model. The intercept of the model with sei, vi, ninv or sqrtninv as the predictor is the 'limit estimate' of the effect (the estimate under infinite precision), see RegtestResult.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult | FixedBinaryResult | ArrayLike | str

a fitted model (rma_uni result, or a fixed-effects rma_mh / rma_peto result with model='lm'; model='rma' raises for the latter two, as in metafor), or the observed effect sizes (array-like, or the name of a column of data).

required vi ArrayLike | str | None

sampling variances of a vector x (array-like or column name of data); ignored with a warning when x is a model.

None sei ArrayLike | str | None

standard errors, used when vi is not given.

None ni ArrayLike | str | None

sample sizes (array-like or column name of data), needed for the predictors based on ni. For a model it must have the length of the original data set and defaults to the sample sizes stored in the model. For a vector x it must have the length of x and defaults to the sample sizes stored by escalc.

None subset ArrayLike | None

0-based integer indices or boolean mask of the studies to use (vector input only).

None data DataFrame | None

data frame in which string values of x, vi, sei and ni are looked up as column names.

None model Literal['lm', 'rma']

'rma' | 'lm'. 'rma' (default) fits a meta-regression model (a mixed-effects model for a random-effects x), 'lm' the weighted regression with multiplicative dispersion (the classical Egger test).

'rma' predictor Literal['sei', 'vi', 'ni', 'ninv', 'sqrtni', 'sqrtninv']

'sei' | 'vi' | 'ni' | 'ninv' | 'sqrtni' | 'sqrtninv': the standard error (default), the sampling variance, the sample size, its inverse, its square root or the inverse of its square root. The last four need ni.

'sei' ret_fit bool

whether the printed summary also shows the fitted regression model (fit is in the result either way). It prints nothing extra for model='lm', which has no fit.

False digits int | None

number of decimals used when the result is printed. Default None: the digits of the model, or 4.

None level float | None

confidence level of the interval of the limit estimate and of the model fit, between 0 and 100 (as in metafor's level: 95 or 0.95 give a 95% interval, and a value up to 0.5 is read as the significance level). Default None: the level of the model, or 95.

None method str | None

tau^2 estimator of the meta-regression model, e.g. 'REML', 'DL' or 'FE'. Default None: the method of x, or 'REML' for a vector. For model='lm' it is only recorded in the result.

None test str | None

test for the model coefficients: 'z' | 't' | 'knha' | 'adhoc'. Default None: the test of x, or 'z' for a vector. Ignored for model='lm', which always uses a t-test.

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

what to do with studies with missing values in a vector x: 'omit' | 'exclude' | 'pass' omit them with a warning, 'fail' raises. It has no effect on a fitted model.

docs.text:
trimfill(
    x: RMAResult,
    side: Literal['left', 'right'] | None = None,
    estimator: Literal['L0', 'R0', 'Q0'] = 'L0',
    maxiter: int = 100,
    verbose: bool = False,
    ilim: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> TrimfillResult

Trim-and-fill method for a model without moderators.

Mirrors metafor's trimfill. The number of studies missing from one side of the funnel plot is estimated (Duval & Tweedie, 2000, doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2000.00455.x), the corresponding mirror-image studies are filled in, and the model is refitted to the observed and the filled-in studies.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult

a fitted equal- or random-effects model (rma_uni result) without moderators.

required side Literal['left', 'right'] | None

'left' | 'right': the side of the funnel plot on which studies are missing. Default None: determined from the sign of the slope of a regression of the effect sizes on their standard errors (the 'right' side if it is negative).

None estimator Literal['L0', 'R0', 'Q0']

'L0' | 'R0' | 'Q0': the estimator of the number of missing studies (default 'L0').

'L0' maxiter int

maximum number of iterations of the algorithm (default 100); an error is raised when it does not converge.

100 verbose bool

whether to print the iterations (number of missing studies and estimate) to stdout.

False ilim tuple[float, float] | None

(lower, upper) limits to which the effect sizes of the augmented data set are clipped; as in metafor's code this includes the observed effect sizes as well as the filled-in ones, and it is only applied when studies are filled in. Must have two elements. Default None: no clipping.

None **kwargs Any

level and test are passed on to the model fits; other keywords are ignored (metafor passes all extra arguments to rma.uni).

{}

Returns:

Type Description TrimfillResult

A TrimfillResult: the refitted model (all the attributes of an RMAResult) with the

TrimfillResult

additional fields fill (flags the filled-in studies, which come last), k0, se_k0, side, k0_est and p_k0. If no study is

TrimfillResult

missing (k0 == 0) the model is that of x.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid, x has moderators, k = 1, or the algorithm fails or does not converge.

ArgumentError

x is not an rma_uni result (for example an rma_mh result or a vector).

NotSupportedError

x is a robust fit, a location-scale model or a selection model.

docs.title: fsn
docs.text:
fsn(
    x: RMAResult | ArrayLike | str,
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    *,
    sei: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | None = None,
    data: DataFrame | None = None,
    type: Literal[
        'Rosenthal',
        'Orwin',
        'Rosenberg',
        'General',
        'Binomial',
    ]
    | None = None,
    alpha: float = 0.05,
    target: float | None = None,
    method: str | None = None,
    exact: bool = False,
    verbose: bool | int = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    pool: Literal['stouffer', 'fisher'] = 'stouffer',
    mumiss: float = 0,
    interval: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    maxint: float = 10000000.0,
    tol: float = EPS**0.25,
    maxiter: int = 1000,
    tau2: float | None = None,
    test: str | None = None,
    weighted: bool | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    rng: RRandom | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> FsnResult

Fail-safe N calculation.

Mirrors metafor's fsn. It computes the number of studies averaging a null result that would have to be added to a set of studies to reduce the significance level to a target value (or the average effect to a target size). The approaches (type) are Rosenthal's (1979, doi:10.1037/0033-2909.86.3.638), Orwin's (1983, doi:10.3102/10769986008002157), Rosenberg's (2005, doi:10.1111/j.0014-3820.2005.tb01004.x), a general approach that refits a random-effects model, and 'Binomial'. 'Binomial' is not on metafor's help page, but metafor's code (R/fsn.r, also in 5.2-1) has it: it takes the number of studies with a positive estimate, applies the two-sided exact binomial (sign) test of a probability of 0.5 and adds studies in pairs, one with a positive and one with a non-positive estimate, until the p-value reaches alpha; the fail-safe N is the number of studies added (0 if the observed p-value is already at least alpha).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult | ArrayLike | str

either a fitted model without moderators (then type='General' is used) or the observed effect sizes (array-like, or the name of a column of data).

required vi ArrayLike | str | None

sampling variances of a vector x (array-like or column name of data); a single value is repeated for all studies. Ignored with a warning when x is a model. Required for the 'Rosenthal', 'Rosenberg' and 'General' types. For 'Orwin' the average is weighted by 1/vi when vi or sei is given (and weighted is not False), else it is the unweighted average. For 'Binomial' the values are not used (metafor's code asks for them, here they are optional).

None sei ArrayLike | str | None

standard errors, used when vi is not given.

None subset ArrayLike | None

0-based integer indices or boolean mask of the studies to use (vector input only).

None data DataFrame | None

data frame in which string values of x, vi and sei are looked up as column names.

None type Literal['Rosenthal', 'Orwin', 'Rosenberg', 'General', 'Binomial'] | None

'Rosenthal' | 'Orwin' | 'Rosenberg' | 'General' | 'Binomial' (case-insensitive; a leading part of a name is enough, the first match in the order Rosenthal, Binomial, Orwin, Rosenberg, General is taken). Default None: 'Rosenthal' for a vector, always 'General' for a model (with a warning if another type is given).

None alpha float

target significance level (default 0.05) for the Rosenthal, Rosenberg, Binomial and General types.

0.05 target float | None

target average effect size for the 'Orwin' and 'General' types; ignored by the other types. A target of the opposite sign to the observed average has its sign flipped, and a target of 0 gives an infinite fail-safe N. Default None: for 'Orwin' half of the average effect size (so the fail-safe N is k), for 'General' the p-value criterion alpha is used instead of a target.

None method str | None

tau^2 estimator of the random-effects model of the 'General' type, e.g. 'REML'. Default None: the method of x, or 'REML'.

None exact bool

for the 'General' type, whether the file-drawer studies are generated as random normal deviates (scaled to have the mean mumiss) and the model refitted (True), or the faster approximation is used (default False). The approximation is used anyway when the number of file-drawer studies exceeds 5000. It is set to True when test is not 'z'.

False verbose bool | int

print the steps of the search for the fail-safe N, and pass on to the model fit.

False digits int | None

number of decimals used when the result is printed. Default None: the digits of the model, or 4.

None pool Literal['stouffer', 'fisher']

'stouffer' | 'fisher': how the p-values are combined for the 'Rosenthal' type (default 'stouffer').

'stouffer' mumiss float

average effect of the file-drawer studies for the 'General' type (default 0).

0 interval tuple[float, float] | None

(lower, upper) initial interval of the root search for the fail-safe N, which is extended if the root lies outside it. Default None: 0 to 50 times the number of studies.

None maxint float

largest fail-safe N that is returned; larger values are reported as '>' that value (default 1e7).

10000000.0 tol float

tolerance of the root finding (default eps**0.25).

EPS ** 0.25 maxiter int

maximum number of iterations of the root finding (default 1000).

1000 tau2 float | None

fixed value of tau^2 for the 'General' type. Default None: estimated (or the fixed value of a model x).

None test str | None

test for the 'General' type: 'z' | 't' | 'knha' | 'adhoc'. Default None: the test of x, or 'z'.

None weighted bool | None

whether weighted estimation is used for the 'General' type (for 'Orwin', False gives the unweighted average, True requires vi or sei). Default None: that of x, or True ('Orwin': weighted if vi or sei is given).

None seed int | None

seed of the R-compatible random number generator used for exact=True (see set_seed).

None rng RRandom | None

an existing generator to use instead of the global one.

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

what to do with studies with missing values in a vector x: 'omit' | 'exclude' | 'pass' omit them with a warning, 'fail' raises. It has no effect on a fitted model.

'omit'

Returns:

Type Description FsnResult

An FsnResult with the fail-safe N fsnum (infinite if the target is 0), the approach used type, the average

FsnResult

effect est, tau2, pval, alpha and target, and, for the 'General' type, the values with the file drawer (est_fsn,

FsnResult

tau2_fsn, pval_fsn). The fail-safe N is 0 if the observed result already meets the criterion.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid, the model has moderators or custom weights, k = 1, or a sampling variance is not positive, or studies are missing and na_action='fail'.

NotSupportedError

x is a model other than an rma_uni result (for example rma_mh, rma_peto, rma_mv, rma_glmm, rma_ls, selection models and robust fits).

docs.title: hc
docs.text:
hc(
    obj: RMAResult,
    digits: int | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    control: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> HcResult

Henmi and Copas pooled estimate and confidence interval for a random-effects model.

Mirrors metafor's hc. The pooled estimate uses the inverse-variance weights of an equal-effects model, which do not depend on the amount of heterogeneity; the heterogeneity is estimated with the DerSimonian-Laird estimator and enters the standard error and the confidence interval (Henmi & Copas, 2010, doi:10.1002/sim.4029).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default obj RMAResult

a fitted equal- or random-effects model (rma_uni result) without moderators.

required digits int | None

number of decimals used when the result is printed. Default None: the digits of obj.

None transf Callable[..., Any] | None

function applied to the estimate and the confidence interval bounds (e.g. metafopy.transf.ilogit). The standard errors are then NaN. Default None: no transformation.

None targs Any

additional argument for transf, passed as its second argument (for the integral and mode transformations, a mapping with tau2, defaulting to the tau^2 of obj).

None control dict[str, Any] | None

mapping with tol (tolerance of the root search, default eps**0.25) and maxiter (default 1000); other keys are ignored.

None

Returns:

Type Description HcResult

An HcResult with the estimate beta, standard error se and bounds ci_lb, ci_ub of the Henmi-Copas

HcResult

interval and the tau^2 estimate tau2 it is based on, and the same quantities of the conventional model (beta_rma, se_rma,

HcResult

ci_lb_rma, ci_ub_rma, tau2_rma, method_rma).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid, obj has moderators, k = 1, a sampling variance is not positive, or the root search fails.

ArgumentError

obj is not an rma_uni result.

NotSupportedError

obj is a location-scale model or a selection model.

Ioannidis & Trikalinos (2007), doi:10.1177/1740774507079441. The power of each study is evaluated at an assumed true effect (by default the weighted average); the observed number of significant results is compared with the expected one. See https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/tes.html.

docs.title: tes
docs.text:
tes(
    x: RMAResult
    | RMAMVResult
    | FixedBinaryResult
    | RMALSResult
    | SelmodelResult
    | GLMMResult
    | ArrayLike
    | str,
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    *,
    sei: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | None = None,
    data: DataFrame | None = None,
    H0: float = 0.0,
    alternative: Literal[
        'two.sided', 'greater', 'less'
    ] = 'two.sided',
    alpha: float = 0.05,
    theta: ArrayLike | None = None,
    tau2: float | None = None,
    test: Literal['chi2', 'binom', 'exact'] | None = None,
    tes_alternative: Literal[
        'two.sided', 'greater', 'less'
    ] = 'greater',
    tes_alpha: float = 0.1,
    progbar: bool = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    correct: bool = False,
    rel_tol: float = EPS**0.25,
    subdivisions: int = 100,
    tau2_lb: float = 0.0,
    find_lim: bool = True,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> TesResult

Test of excess significance.

Mirrors metafor's tes. The power of each study is computed for an assumed true effect and the observed number of significant studies is compared with the expected number (Ioannidis & Trikalinos, 2007, doi:10.1177/1740774507079441). Also estimates the true effect theta_lim at which the test would be just significant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult | ArrayLike | str

a fitted model (the power is based on its estimate, or its fitted values with moderators, and its tau^2; then vi, sei, subset, theta and tau2 are ignored, without a warning), or the observed effect sizes (array-like, or the name of a column of data).

required vi ArrayLike | str | None

sampling variances of a vector x (array-like or column name of data).

None sei ArrayLike | str | None

standard errors, used when vi is not given. One of vi and sei is required for a vector x.

None subset ArrayLike | None

0-based integer indices or boolean mask of the studies to use (vector input only).

None data DataFrame | None

data frame in which string values of x, vi and sei are looked up as column names.

None H0 float

value of the effect under the null hypothesis of the significance tests of the studies (default 0).

0.0 alternative Literal['two.sided', 'greater', 'less']

'two.sided' | 'greater' | 'less': the alternative of the significance tests of the studies (default 'two.sided'). Unlike in metafor, abbreviations are not accepted (also for test and tes_alternative).

'two.sided' alpha float

significance level of those tests (default 0.05).

0.05 theta ArrayLike | None

assumed true effect, a single value or one per study. Default None: the inverse-variance weighted average of the effects (with weights 1/(vi + tau2) when tau2 is used).

None tau2 float | None

amount of heterogeneity in the true effects; the power of each study is then averaged over a normal distribution of the true effects with mean theta and variance tau2. Default None: homogeneous true effects. A value not above tau2_lb counts as none.

None test Literal['chi2', 'binom', 'exact'] | None

'chi2' | 'binom' | 'exact': the test of excess significance (chi-square, binomial or exact test). Default None: 'exact' if the number of terms in the sum of the exact test, the sum of the binomial coefficients choose(k, j) over the j involved (all j for tes_alternative='two.sided', j >= O for 'greater', j <= O for 'less'), is at most 10^6, else 'chi2'. The exact test is computed here without listing the combinations, so test='exact' also works for a large number of studies, where metafor stops.

None tes_alternative Literal['two.sided', 'greater', 'less']

'two.sided' | 'greater' | 'less': the alternative of the test of excess significance (default 'greater').

'greater' tes_alpha float

significance level of the test of excess significance, used for theta_lim (default 0.1).

0.1 progbar bool

whether to show a progress bar on stderr during the exact test (metafor's default is True, here it is False).

False digits int | None

number of decimals used when the result is printed. Default None: the digits of the model, or 4.

None correct bool

whether the continuity correction of the chi-square test is used (default False).

False rel_tol float

tolerance (absolute and relative) of the numerical integration of the power over the distribution of the true effects (default eps**0.25).

EPS ** 0.25 subdivisions int

maximum number of subdivisions of that integration (default 100).

100 tau2_lb float

tau2 values not above this lower bound are treated as zero (default 0).

0.0 find_lim bool

whether theta_lim is estimated (default True; only when theta is a single value or estimated).

True na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

what to do with studies with missing values in a vector x: 'omit' | 'exclude' | 'pass' omit them with a warning, 'fail' raises. It has no effect on a fitted model.

'omit'

Returns:

Type Description TesResult

A TesResult with the number of studies k, the observed number O and expected number E of significant

TesResult

studies, their ratio OEratio, the test used test with its statistic X2 (chi-square test only) and p-value pval, the power

TesResult

of each study power, the significance flags sig, the assumed effect theta and the limit estimate theta_lim.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid, or studies are missing and na_action='fail'.

NotSupportedError

x is a model of a class tes is not available for (for example rma_mv, rma_glmm, rma_ls, selection models and robust fits).

Metafor reference

tes

Names of the bundled datasets.

The datasets were exported from the R package metadat (https://wviechtb.github.io/metadat/): every data frame it provided when they were exported, plus the data of Moura et al. (2021) and its phylogenetic tree. A few datasets listed on the metadat site are not bundled, and the list can include dat.berkey1998r, which is not in the site index.

A rooted tree stored as an edge table, like the phylo class of the R package ape.

Tips are the nodes that are never a parent; the tips are taken in the order of their node ids (as in ape, and as in the bundled tree, the tips have the ids 1 to the number of tips).

    flip: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    include: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    add: float | None = None,
    to: Literal['all', 'only0', 'if0all', 'none'] = 'only0',
    drop00: bool = False,
    vtype: str | Sequence[str] = 'LS',
    correct: bool | str = True,
    cutoff: float | None = None,
    var_names: Sequence[str] = ('yi', 'vi'),
    add_measure: bool = False,
    append: bool = True,
    replace: bool = True,
    digits: int | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    onlyo1: bool = False,

    addvi: bool = True,
) -> DataFrame

Calculate effect sizes yi and sampling variances vi (metafor's escalc).

The metafor reference (last section) lists the measures, the arguments each one needs and the vtype options. add defaults to 1/2, except for the measures where metafor uses 0 (AS, PHI, ZPHI, RTET, ZTET, IRSD, PAS, PFT, IRS, IRFT).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default measure str | None

Effect size or outcome measure to compute, a metafor code such as 'SMD', 'OR', 'RR', 'ZCOR' or 'PR'; see the metafor reference (last section) for the full list. Which of the data arguments below are needed depends on the measure. None (with yi) means 'GEN'.

None ai ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table frequencies (upper left cell).

None bi ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table frequencies (upper right cell).

None ci ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table frequencies (lower left cell).

None di ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table frequencies (lower right cell).

None n1i ArrayLike | str | None

Group sizes or row totals (first group or row).

None n2i ArrayLike | str | None

Group sizes or row totals (second group or row).

None x1i ArrayLike | str | None

Number of events (first group).

None x2i ArrayLike | str | None

Number of events (second group).

None t1i ArrayLike | str | None

Total person-times (first group).

None t2i ArrayLike | str | None

Total person-times (second group).

None m1i ArrayLike | str | None

Means (first group or time point).

None m2i ArrayLike | str | None

Means (second group or time point).

None sd1i ArrayLike | str | None

Standard deviations (first group or time point).

None sd2i ArrayLike | str | None

Standard deviations (second group or time point).

None xi ArrayLike | str | None

Frequencies of the event of interest.

None mi ArrayLike | str | None

Frequencies of the complement of the event of interest, or the group means.

None ri ArrayLike | str | None

Raw correlation coefficients.

None ti ArrayLike | str | None

Total person-times or t-test statistics.

None fi ArrayLike | str | None

F-test statistics.

None pi ArrayLike | str | None

(Signed) p-values.

None sdi ArrayLike | str | None

Standard deviations.

None r2i ArrayLike | str | None

R^2 values.

None mini ArrayLike | str | None

Minimum values.

None maxi ArrayLike | str | None

Maximum values.

None ni ArrayLike | str | None

Sample or group sizes.

None yi ArrayLike | str | None

Effect size estimates, for measure='GEN' (used as they are, with vi or sei).

None vi ArrayLike | str | None

Sampling variances matching yi.

None sei ArrayLike | str | None

Standard errors matching yi; vi is their square. Ignored when vi is given.

None data DataFrame | Mapping[str, ArrayLike] | None

Data frame (or mapping of columns) holding the variables named in the data arguments. Each of the arguments above is then an array or the name of a column of data.

None slab ArrayLike | str | None

Study labels, as a sequence or a column name. Stored in attrs['slab'].

None flip ArrayLike | str | None

Flip the sign of the estimates: a boolean (or a boolean per study), or a numeric multiplier (one per study), or the name of a column of data. The sampling variances are multiplied by the square of the multiplier.

None subset ArrayLike | str | None

Studies to keep in the returned frame: a boolean array, 0-based indices or an expression string evaluated on data.

None include ArrayLike | str | None

Studies for which the measure is computed (the others get missing values), given like subset.

None add float | None

Non-negative amount to add to zero cells, counts or frequencies. Default 0.5 (0 for the measures listed above).

None to Literal['all', 'only0', 'if0all', 'none']

When add is added: 'only0' (to the table of a study with a zero cell, the default), 'all', 'if0all' (to all tables when any has a zero cell) or 'none'.

'only0' drop00 bool

Drop studies with no cases or events (or only cases) in both groups from the calculations (set their values to missing). Used for the 2x2 table measures and 'IRR', 'IRD' and 'IRSD' only.

False vtype str | Sequence[str]

Type of sampling variance: one of 'UB', 'LS' (the default), 'LS2', 'LS3', 'HO', 'ST', 'CS', 'AV', 'AV2', 'AVHO', 'H0', 'H0a', 'H0b' or 'MAX'. The valid options depend on the measure; a sequence gives one type per study.

'LS' correct bool | str

Apply the bias correction to the estimates (default True), for the measures that have one ('SMD', 'SMD1', 'SMDH', 'SMD1H', 'ROM', 'VR', 'CVR', 'SMN', 'SDLN', 'CVLN', 'SMCC', 'SMCR', 'SMCRH', 'SMCRP', 'SMCRPH', 'ROMC' and 'CVRC'); it has no effect on the others. For the measures built on cmicalc ('SMD', 'SMD1', 'SMDH', 'SMD1H', 'SMN', 'SMCC', 'SMCR', 'SMCRH', 'SMCRP', 'SMCRPH') it may also be 'exact' (the same as True) or 'approx'; ROM, VR, CVR, SDLN, CVLN, ROMC and CVRC need a bool.

True cutoff float | None

Absolute value above which a computed estimate is flagged with a warning. The default is 2 for 'SMD', 'SMDH', 'SMD1' and 'SMD1H' and no check for the other measures; NaN switches the check off. A given set of estimates is flagged once per session.

None var_names Sequence[str]

Names of the estimate and sampling variance columns of the result (('yi', 'vi'); a third name with add_measure).

('yi', 'vi') add_measure bool

Add a column recording the measure computed (named 'measure' unless var_names has a third entry).

False append bool

Return data with the new columns appended (True, the default) or only the new columns.

summary_escalc(
    object: DataFrame,
    out_names: Sequence[str] = (
        'sei',
        'zi',
        'pval',
        'ci.lb',
        'ci.ub',
    ),
    var_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    H0: ArrayLike = 0,
    append: bool = True,
    replace: bool = True,
    level: float = 95,
    olim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    digits: int | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> DataFrame

Add standard errors, test statistics, p-values and confidence intervals to the output of escalc.

Mirrors metafor's summary.escalc. With yi and vi the effect sizes and sampling variances, it computes sei = sqrt(vi), zi = (yi - H0) / sei, the two-sided p-value pval and the Wald-type interval yi -/+ z_crit * sei. With transf, yi and the bounds are transformed (the bounds are put in increasing order) and vi, sei, zi and pval are dropped.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default object DataFrame

data frame returned by escalc (or a frame with the effect sizes and sampling variances as columns).

required out_names Sequence[str]

names of the five new columns, in the order standard error, test statistic, p-value, lower and upper bound (default 'sei', 'zi', 'pval', 'ci.lb', 'ci.ub').

('sei', 'zi', 'pval', 'ci.lb', 'ci.ub') var_names Sequence[str] | None

names of the columns with the effect sizes and the sampling variances (two names). Default None: taken from the attributes of object, else 'yi' and 'vi'.

None H0 ArrayLike

value of the effect under the null hypothesis for zi and pval, a scalar or one value per row (default 0).

0 append bool

whether the new columns are appended to object (default True); otherwise only the effect sizes (and sampling variances) and the new columns are returned.

True replace bool

whether existing columns with the names in out_names are replaced (default True); if False only their missing values are filled in.

True level float

confidence level in percent, between 0 and 100 (default 95).

95 olim Sequence[float] | None

(lower, upper) limits to which yi and the bounds are clipped; zi and pval are based on the unclipped values. Default None: no clipping.

None digits int | Sequence[int] | None

number of decimals used when the frame is printed; stored in attrs['digits']. Default None: the digits of object.

None transf Callable[..., Any] | None

function applied to the effect sizes and the bounds, for example metafopy.transf.ilogit. Default None.

None **kwargs Any

additional arguments passed on to transf.

{}

A data frame with the columns of object and the new columns named by out_names (or yi, vi, and the new columns when

DataFrame

append=False). The escalc attributes (measure, slab, ni, ...) are kept, except when transf is given: the result then

DataFrame

cmicalc(
    mi: ArrayLike, method: bool | str = 'exact'
) -> NDArray[float64]

Small-sample bias correction factor for standardized mean differences.

Mirrors metafor's cmicalc. The factor c(m) of Hedges (1981, doi:10.3102/10769986006002107) multiplies a standardized mean difference to remove its small-sample bias. escalc uses it for the measures SMD, SMD1, SMDH, SMD1H, SMN, SMCC, SMCR, SMCRH, SMCRP and SMCRPH, passing its argument correct as method.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mi ArrayLike

degrees of freedom m (for example n1i + n2i - 2), scalar or array-like.

required method bool | str

'exact' | 'approx' | True | False. 'exact' (or True, the default) uses the gamma-function form, 'approx' the approximation 1 - 3/(4m - 1), and False applies no correction (a factor of 1). Strings can be abbreviated; an empty string or None raises.

'exact'

Returns:

Type Description NDArray[float64]

Array of the factors c(m) with the shape of mi; with 'exact' or 'approx', NaN where m <= 1 (or mi is missing).

method is None, or a string that is not an abbreviation of 'exact' or 'approx'.

predict_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    newmods: ArrayLike
    | Mapping[str, float]
    | Series
    | DataFrame
    | PairmatSpec
    | None = None,
    *,
    intercept: bool | None = None,
    tau2_levels: Sequence[str | int]
    | str
    | int
    | None = None,
    gamma2_levels: Sequence[str | int]
    | str
    | int
    | None = None,
    hetvar: ArrayLike | None = None,
    prob: str | float | None = None,
    addx: bool = False,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    adjust: bool = False,
    vcov: bool = False,
    predtype: str | None = None,
    pi_type: str | None = None,
    newvi: ArrayLike | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> PredictResult

Predicted values, standard errors, confidence intervals and prediction intervals for an rma_uni fit.

Without newmods an intercept-only model gives the pooled estimate and a meta-regression the fitted value of each study.

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/predict.rma.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMAResult

Model fitted by rma_uni.

required newmods ArrayLike | Mapping[str, float] | Series | DataFrame | PairmatSpec | None

Moderator values of new studies to predict for, without the intercept column (it is added, see intercept) or with all p columns (then intercept is ignored, with a warning if given, and the first column decides whether the intercept is included). A number or 1-d array gives one prediction per value if the model has a single moderator and one prediction otherwise; a 2-d array gives one prediction per row. A dict, pandas Series or DataFrame with string names is matched by name to the moderators of the model when it has more than one moderator (a name may be shortened to any subsequence of the moderator name, as in metafor). The predictions are labelled by the index of a DataFrame with string index, or by the names of a dict or Series for a model with a single moderator, else by their position. A pairmat specification is also accepted. Factors must be given as the contrast variables of the model matrix. Models without moderators do not accept newmods. Default: no new values, so an intercept-only model gives the pooled estimate and a meta-regression the fitted value of every study.

None intercept bool | None

Whether to include the intercept when predicting for newmods: if False, the intercept column is set to 0. Default: the column of ones is added if the model has an intercept. Ignored when newmods has all p columns.

None tau2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

Levels of the inner factor for the prediction interval. Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect for this model.

None gamma2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

Levels of the inner factor for the prediction interval. Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect for this model.

None hetvar ArrayLike | None

Amount of heterogeneity to use in the prediction interval instead of the estimated tau^2: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). Default: the estimate of the model.

None prob str | float | None

Probability to add to the result, as a string such as '>0.2' or '<0': the probability that a true outcome is above (>) or below (<) the cutoff, from the predictive distribution (normal or t, see predtype). A number means >. The cutoff may be an arithmetic expression (+ - * / ^) using the constants pi and Inf and the functions abs, atanh, cos, exp, log, log10, log1p, log2, plogis, qlogis, sin, sqrt, tan and tanh, such as '>log(0.8)'; a string that is not such an expression gives no prob, as in metafor. Cannot be combined with adjust=True. Default: none.

None addx bool

Add the model matrix of the predictions to the result (X).

False transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to each predicted value and interval bound separately (for example numpy.exp); se is then NaN and the lower and upper bounds are put in order. Default: no transformation.

None targs Any

Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none, except for the integral and mode transformations of transf, which get {'tau2': tau2}.

None level float | None

Confidence and prediction interval level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

None adjust bool

Apply a Bonferroni correction: the significance level is divided by the number of predictions, which widens the intervals.

False vcov bool

Add the variance-covariance matrix of the predictions to the result (vcov; metafor returns it as a second list element). Ignored with transf.

False predtype str | None

Type of prediction interval: 'default' (the normal distribution, or the t distribution with the degrees of freedom ddf of the test), 'simple' (ignore the uncertainty of the predicted value, normal distribution), 'riley' (t distribution with ddf - parms + p degrees of freedom, which is k - parms when ddf = k - p; Riley et al., 2011, doi:10.1136/bmj.d549) or 't' (t distribution with ddf degrees of freedom); degrees of freedom below 1 are set to 1. Case is ignored and a unique prefix is accepted. Default: pi_type, else 'default'.

None pi_type str | None

Old spelling of predtype, used when predtype is None.

None newvi ArrayLike | None

Sampling variances of the new studies, added to the variance of the prediction interval: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). Default: 0.

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

What to do with studies left out of the fit because of missing values: 'omit', 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail' (metafor takes this from the na.action option). For the fitted values (no newmods) of a meta-regression, 'omit' returns the studies used in fitting, 'exclude' one row per study with NaN for those left out and 'pass' one row per study computed from the moderator values it has. 'fail' raises if any study was left out of the fit, also when newmods is given. Predictions for newmods drop ('omit') or keep ('exclude', 'pass') the rows that are NaN.

'omit' digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

Number of decimals used when printing, or a mapping with any of the keys est, se, test, pval, ci, var, sevar, fit and het (a unique prefix of a key is accepted). It is stored in the result and does not change the values. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None verbose bool

Accepted for metafor's printing of the details of a failing clubSandwich contrast; it has no effect here.

False

Returns:

Type Description PredictResult

The predictions, a PredictResult with pred, se, ci_lb, ci_ub, pi_lb and pi_ub (one entry per

PredictResult

prediction; the prediction interval is NaN where there is none), plus prob, X and vcov if requested. Unlike metafor, vcov is a

PredictResult

field of the result, not a second list element.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid (for example prob with adjust=True, newmods of the wrong width or for a model without moderators, an unknown predtype or na_action, a hetvar or newvi of the wrong length, or a fit made robust with club_sandwich=True and the saddlepoint test).

The predictions are labelled by the index of a DataFrame with string index, or by the names of a dict or Series for a model with a single moderator, else by their position. A pairmat specification is also accepted. Factors must be given as the contrast variables of the model matrix. Models without moderators do not accept newmods. Default: no new values, so an intercept-only model gives the pooled estimate and a meta-regression the fitted value of every study.

None intercept bool | None

Whether to include the intercept when predicting for newmods: if False, the intercept column is set to 0. Default: the column of ones is added if the model has an intercept. Ignored when newmods has all p columns.

None tau2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

Which tau2 value(s) to use in the prediction interval when the model has several: labels of the inner factor of the first inner | outer term or 0-based positions (a single value, used for every prediction, or a sequence with one per prediction). Default: none. With newmods and several tau2 values the prediction intervals are then NaN (metafor requires the levels). With the fitted values of a meta-regression the levels are those of the studies and tau2_levels is ignored (with a warning). For an intercept-only model metafor then returns one prediction for each tau2 value, whereas metafopy returns a single prediction with a NaN prediction interval.

None gamma2_levels Sequence[str | int] | str | int | None

As tau2_levels, for the gamma2 values (second inner | outer term).

None hetvar ArrayLike | None

Amount of heterogeneity to use in the prediction interval instead of the sum of the variance components: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). tau2_levels and gamma2_levels are then ignored (with a warning).

None prob str | float | None

Probability to add to the result, as a string such as '>0.2' or '<0': the probability that a true outcome is above (>) or below (<) the cutoff, from the predictive distribution (normal or t, see predtype). A number means >. The cutoff may be an arithmetic expression (+ - * / ^) using the constants pi and Inf and the functions abs, atanh, cos, exp, log, log10, log1p, log2, plogis, qlogis, sin, sqrt, tan and tanh, such as '>log(0.8)'; a string that is not such an expression gives no prob, as in metafor. Cannot be combined with adjust=True. Default: none.

None addx bool

Add the model matrix of the predictions to the result (X).

False transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to each predicted value and interval bound separately (for example numpy.exp); se is then NaN and the lower and upper bounds are put in order. Default: no transformation.

None targs Any

Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none, except for the integral and mode transformations of transf, which get {'tau2': tau2}.

None level float | None

Confidence and prediction interval level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

None adjust bool

Apply a Bonferroni correction: the significance level is divided by the number of predictions, which widens the intervals.

False vcov bool

Add the variance-covariance matrix of the predictions to the result (vcov; metafor returns it as a second list element). Ignored with transf.

False predtype str | None

Type of prediction interval: 'default' (the normal distribution, or the t distribution with the degrees of freedom ddf of the test), 'simple' (ignore the uncertainty of the predicted value, normal distribution), 'riley' (t distribution with ddf - parms + p degrees of freedom, which is k - parms when ddf = k - p; Riley et al., 2011, doi:10.1136/bmj.d549) or 't' (t distribution with ddf degrees of freedom); degrees of freedom below 1 are set to 1. Case is ignored and a unique prefix is accepted. Default: pi_type, else 'default'.

None pi_type str | None

Old spelling of predtype, used when predtype is None.

None newvi ArrayLike | None

Sampling variances of the new studies, added to the variance of the prediction interval: a number or one value per prediction (a different length raises InputError). Default: 0.

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

What to do with studies left out of the fit because of missing values: 'omit', 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail' (metafor takes this from the na.action option). For the fitted values (no newmods) of a meta-regression, 'omit' returns the studies used in fitting, 'exclude' one row per study with NaN for those left out and 'pass' one row per study computed from the moderator values it has. 'fail' raises if any study was left out of the fit, also when newmods is given. Predictions for newmods drop ('omit') or keep ('exclude', 'pass') the rows that are NaN.

'omit' digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

Number of decimals used when printing, or a mapping with any of the keys est, se, test, pval, ci, var, sevar, fit and het (a unique prefix of a key is accepted). It is stored in the result and does not change the values. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None verbose bool

Accepted for metafor's printing of the details of a failing clubSandwich contrast; it has no effect here.

False

Returns:

Type Description PredictResult

The predictions, a PredictResult with pred, se, ci_lb, ci_ub, pi_lb and pi_ub (one entry per

PredictResult

prediction; the prediction interval is NaN where there is none), plus prob, X and vcov if requested. Unlike metafor, vcov is a

PredictResult

field of the result, not a second list element.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid (for example newmods for a model without moderators, a level in tau2_levels or gamma2_levels that does not exist or a sequence of the wrong length, prob with adjust=True, an unknown predtype or na_action, or a hetvar or newvi of the wrong length).

Metafor reference

predict.rma

docs.title: predict_rma_ls
docs.text:
predict_rma_ls(
    model: RMALSResult,
    newmods: ArrayLike | PairmatSpec | None = None,
    *,
    intercept: bool | None = None,
    addx: bool = False,
    newscale: ArrayLike | None = None,
    addz: bool = False,
    prob: str | None = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    adjust: bool = False,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    vcov: bool = False,
    predtype: str | None = None,
    pi_type: str | None = None,
    newvi: ArrayLike | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> LSPredictResult

Predicted values for a location-scale model, fitted by rma_uni with scale (metafor's predict.rma.ls).

What is predicted depends on the arguments. Without newmods and newscale the result holds the fitted values of the studies, with prediction intervals that use the tau^2 of each study. With newmods only it holds the predicted effects with confidence intervals; the prediction intervals are NaN, since tau^2 is not known for the new studies. With both it holds the predicted effects with confidence and prediction intervals, using the tau^2 predicted from newscale. With newscale only, pred holds the predicted log(tau^2) (log link) or tau^2 (identity link), pred_type is 'scale' and the prediction intervals are NaN (use transf=numpy.exp for tau^2 under the log link). With the identity link and no transf, negative predicted tau^2 values are set to 0 with a warning.

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/predict.rma.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMALSResult

Location-scale model fitted by rma_uni with scale.

required newmods ArrayLike | PairmatSpec | None

Moderator values of new studies to predict for, without the intercept column (it is added, see intercept) or with all p columns (then intercept is ignored, with a warning if given). A number or 1-d array gives one prediction per value if the model has a single moderator and one prediction otherwise; a 2-d array gives one prediction per row. A dict, pandas Series or DataFrame with string names is matched by name to the moderators of the model when it has more than one moderator (a name may be shortened to any subsequence of the moderator name, as in metafor). A pairmat specification is also accepted. Factors must be given as the contrast variables of the model matrix. A model without moderators accepts only newmods=1. Default: none (the fitted values of the studies if newscale is not given either).

None intercept bool | None

Whether to include the intercept when predicting for newmods (and newscale if newmods is not given): if False, the intercept column is set to 0. Default: the column of ones is added if the model has an intercept. Ignored when the matrix has all its columns; the intercept column of newscale is always 1 when newmods is given too.

None addx bool

Add the model matrix of the predictions to the result (X).

False newscale ArrayLike | None

Values of the scale variables of the new studies, without the intercept column (added, see intercept) or with all q columns; same forms as newmods. A model without scale variables accepts only newscale=1. If both are given, they must have the same number of rows, except that a single row of either is repeated. Default: none (see the description).

None addz bool

Add the model matrix of the scale variables of the predictions to the result (Z).

False prob str | None

Probability to add to the result, as a string such as '>0.2' or '<0': the probability that a true outcome is above (>) or below (<) the cutoff, from the predictive distribution (normal or t, see predtype). The cutoff may be an arithmetic expression as for predict; a string that is not one gives no prob. Not computed for scale predictions (newscale only). Cannot be combined with adjust=True. Default: none.

None level float | None

Confidence and prediction interval level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

None adjust bool

Apply a Bonferroni correction: the significance level is divided by the number of predictions, which widens the intervals.

False transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to each predicted value and interval bound separately (for example numpy.exp); se is then NaN and the lower and upper bounds are put in order. Default: no transformation.

None targs Any

Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none; unlike for predict of an rma_uni fit, the integral and mode transformations get no default tau2.

None vcov bool

Add the variance-covariance matrix of the predictions to the result (vcov; metafor returns it as a second list element). Ignored with transf.

False predtype str | None

Type of prediction interval: 'default' (the normal distribution, or the t distribution with k - p degrees of freedom if the test is 't', 'knha' or 'adhoc'), 'simple' (ignore the uncertainty of the predicted value, normal distribution), 'riley' (t distribution with k - p - q degrees of freedom, Riley et al., 2011, doi:10.1136/bmj.d549) or 't' (t distribution with k - p degrees of freedom); degrees of freedom below 1 are set to 1. Case is ignored and a unique prefix is accepted. Default: pi_type, else 'default'.

None pi_type str | None

Old spelling of predtype, used when predtype is None.

None newvi ArrayLike | None

Sampling variances of the new studies, added to the variance of the prediction interval: a number or one value per prediction. Default: 0.

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

What to do with studies left out of the fit because of missing values: 'omit', 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail' (metafor takes this from the na.action option). For the fitted values (no newmods or newscale), 'omit' returns the studies used in fitting, 'exclude' one row per study with NaN for those left out and 'pass' one row per study computed from the values it has. 'fail' raises if any study was left out of the fit, also when newmods or newscale is given. Predictions for newmods or newscale drop ('omit') or keep ('exclude', 'pass') the rows that are NaN.

'omit' digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

Number of decimals used when printing, or a mapping with any of the keys est, se, test, pval, ci, var, sevar, fit and het (a unique prefix of a key is accepted). It is stored in the result and does not change the values. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None verbose bool

Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect here.

False

Returns:

Type Description LSPredictResult

The predictions, an LSPredictResult: a PredictResult with the extra fields Z (the scale model matrix, with

LSPredictResult

addz=True; None otherwise) and z_names. pred_type is 'location' or 'scale'; the predicted tau^2 of a scale prediction is

LSPredictResult

in pred (there is no tau2 field). ddf is a single number, None if the test is 'z'. Unlike metafor, vcov is a field of the

LSPredictResult

result, not a second list element.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument is invalid (for example prob with adjust=True, an unknown predtype or na_action, a newvi of the wrong length, moderator or scale values for a model without them), or the dimensions of newmods or newscale do not match the model or each other.

Metafor reference

predict.rma

PredictResult(
    pred: FloatArray,
    se: FloatArray,
    ci_lb: FloatArray,
