Predictions with confidence (ci) and prediction (pi) intervals, as returned by predict. Use to_frame() for a data frame and str() for the printout of metafor's print.list.rma.

Attributes:

Name Type Description pred FloatArray

Predicted values, one per prediction.

se FloatArray

Standard errors of the predicted values; NaN when a transformation was applied, as in metafor.

ci_lb FloatArray

Lower bounds of the confidence intervals.

ci_ub FloatArray

Upper bounds of the confidence intervals.

pi_lb FloatArray

Lower bounds of the prediction intervals (cr_lb is an alias); NaN where there is no prediction interval (the equal-effects methods, an integral or mode transformation of an rma_uni or rma_glmm fit).

pi_ub FloatArray

Upper bounds of the prediction intervals (cr_ub is an alias); NaN where there is no prediction interval.

slab tuple[str, ...] | None

Labels of the predictions, or None. A single prediction without a name has the label ''.

pi_se FloatArray | None

Standard errors of the predictions (before any transformation).

pi_dist str | None

Distribution of the prediction, 'norm' or 't' (used by forest(predstyle='shade') and 'dist').

pi_ddf float | FloatArray | None

Degrees of freedom of the prediction distribution, one per prediction; None when pi_dist is 'norm'.

ddf float | FloatArray | None

Degrees of freedom of the confidence intervals, one per prediction (a single number for location-scale models); None when the normal distribution is used (for rma_mv fits: when the prediction interval uses it).

has_pi bool

Whether the model has prediction intervals (False for the equal-effects models of rma_mh and rma_peto).

prob FloatArray | None

Probabilities requested via prob; None if not requested or if the cutoff could not be evaluated.

X FloatArray | DataFrame | None

Model matrix of the predictions (addx=True, else None); a data frame for matreg predictions.

vcov FloatArray | DataFrame | None

Variance-covariance matrix of the predictions (vcov=True without transf, else None); a data frame for matreg predictions.

x_names tuple[str, ...] | None

Column names of X.

digits int

Number of decimals used when printing.

digit_map Mapping[str, int] | None

Decimals by kind of number (est, se, ci, ...), if the digits were given by kind.

method str | None

Estimation method of the model ('FE' for the rma_mh and rma_peto fits).

transf bool

Whether a transformation was applied.

pred_type str

'location' (predicted effects), or 'scale' for the predicted tau^2 values (log(tau^2) with a log link) of a location-scale model.

() **kwargs Any

Any

docs.title: confint_rma_uni
docs.text:
confint_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    *,
    fixed: bool = False,
    random: bool = True,
    type: CIType | None = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    tau2_min: float | None = None,
    tau2_max: float | None = None,
    tol: float = DEFAULT_TOL,
    maxiter: int = 1000,
    verbose: bool | int = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    xlim: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    extint: bool = False,
    parm: Any = None,
) -> ConfintResult

Confidence intervals for the coefficients and for tau^2, I^2 and H^2 of an rma_uni fit (metafor's confint.rma.uni).

The interval for tau^2 is found by root finding (Q-profile, generalised Q, profile likelihood or the Higgins-Thompson method) or is of Wald type; the bounds of I^2 and H^2 follow from those of tau^2.

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/confint.rma.uni.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMAResult

Model fitted by rma_uni.

required fixed bool

Give Wald-type intervals for the coefficients (fixed table of the result), using the t distribution with the degrees of freedom of the test if the model uses it, else the normal distribution.

False random bool

Give intervals for tau^2 (and tau), I^2 and H^2 (random table). At least one of fixed and random must be True.

True type CIType | None

Method for the interval of tau^2 (case is ignored; any other value raises InputError): 'qp' (Q-profile, Viechtbauer, 2007, doi:10.1002/sim.2514; needs positive sampling variances), 'genq' (generalised Q, Jackson, 2013, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1081; needs a GENQ or GENQM fit), 'pl' (profile likelihood, which metafor suggests for ML and REML fits; the likelihood used is the REML one for method='REML' and the ML one otherwise), 'ht' (the test-based method of Higgins and Thompson, 2002, doi:10.1002/sim.1186; only for models without moderators and k > 2), or a Wald type 'wald', 'wald.log' or 'wald.sqrt' (in the metafor source but not described on its reference page). Default: 'genq' for GENQ and GENQM fits, else 'qp'.

None level float | None

Confidence level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

None transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to each coefficient and bound of the fixed table separately, for example numpy.exp; the bounds are put in order. Default: none.

None targs Any

Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none, except for the integral and mode transformations of transf, which get {'tau2': tau2}.

None tau2_min float | None

Lower end of the interval searched for the bounds of tau^2. Default: the smaller of 0 and the estimate (metafor uses the tau2.min of the control of the fitted model instead if it was set; metafopy does not). Replaced by the entry of control or by xlim.

None tau2_max float | None

Upper end of the interval searched for the bounds. Default: the largest of 100, ten times the estimate and ten times the lower end.

None tol float

Convergence tolerance of the root finding (default eps^0.25). Not used for type='genq', which uses the defaults of R's uniroot as metafor does.

DEFAULT_TOL maxiter int

Maximum number of iterations of the root finding (not used for type='genq').

1000 verbose bool | int

Print the steps of the root finding for the types 'qp', 'genq' and 'pl' on stdout, as metafor does; with digits decimals.

False digits int | None

Number of decimals used for verbose output and the printout of the result. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None control Mapping[str, Any] | None

metafor's list of root-finding settings (tau2_min, tau2_max, tol and maxiter, written with . or _). Its entries replace the keyword arguments of the same name. Names must be given in full (metafor accepts partial names); entries that only other functions of metafor read, including verbose, are ignored here, and any other entry raises InputError.

None xlim float | Sequence[float] | None

Interval (tau2_min, tau2_max) searched for the bounds (metafor's ... argument); a single value is the upper limit and the lower one is 0. Wins over control.

None extint bool

Let the search for a profile-likelihood bound (type='pl') widen the interval (R's extendInt; metafor's ... argument).

False parm Any

Ignored, with a warning, as in metafor.

None

Returns:

Type Description ConfintResult

A ConfintResult with the fixed table (coefficients) and/or the random table (tau^2, tau, I^2(%),

ConfintResult

H^2), each with the columns estimate, ci.lb and ci.ub. A bound the search cannot find is NaN, with a warning.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument is invalid (unknown type or control entry, neither fixed nor random, xlim of the wrong length, a search interval that does not contain the estimate for type='pl', type='genq' for a fit that is not GENQ or GENQM, type='ht' with moderators or k <= 2, type='qp' with non-positive sampling variances), k = 1, or the model has no estimated random-effects component (equal-effects methods, or a fixed tau^2).

Metafor reference

confint.rma

docs.title: confint_rma_mv
docs.text:
confint_rma_mv(
    model: RMAMVResult,
    *,
    fixed: bool = False,
    sigma2: int | None = None,
    tau2: int | None = None,
    rho: int | None = None,
    gamma2: int | None = None,
    phi: int | None = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    vc_min: float | None = None,
    vc_max: float | None = None,
    tol: float = DEFAULT_TOL,
    maxiter: int = 1000,
    eptries: int = 10,
    verbose: bool | int = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    extint: bool = False,
    parm: Any = None,
) -> ConfintResult | ConfintList

Confidence intervals for the variance and correlation components, or the coefficients, of an rma_mv fit (metafor's confint.rma.mv).

The intervals of the components are profile-likelihood intervals (Hardy and Thompson, 1996, doi:10.1002/(SICI)1097-0258(19960330)15:6<619::AID-SIM188>3.0.CO;2-A).

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/confint.rma.mv.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMAMVResult

Model fitted by rma_mv.

required fixed bool

Give Wald-type intervals for the coefficients (t distribution with the degrees of freedom of each coefficient unless the test is 'z'). Without a component argument only these are returned; with one, the interval of the component is returned too.

False sigma2 int | None

0-based position of the sigma2 component to compute the interval for. Only one of sigma2, tau2, rho, gamma2 and phi may be given.

None tau2 int | None

0-based position of the tau2 component.

None rho int | None

0-based position of the rho component.

None gamma2 int | None

0-based position of the gamma2 component.

None phi int | None

0-based position of the phi component.

None level float | None

Confidence level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

None transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to each coefficient and bound (with fixed=True) separately; the bounds are put in order. Default: none.

None targs Any

Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none, except for the integral and mode transformations of transf, which get {'tau2': 0}.

None vc_min float | None

Lower end of the interval searched for the bounds of a component. Default: 0 for sigma2, tau2 and gamma2; for rho and phi -1, except min(0, estimate) for the structures 'AR', 'HAR' and 'CAR' and 0 for the spatial structures. Replaced by control or xlim.

None vc_max float | None

Upper end of the interval searched for the bounds. Default: for sigma2, tau2 and gamma2 the larger of 10 and 100 times the estimate (10 if the estimate is practically 0); for rho and phi 1, except max(10, 10 * estimate) for the structures 'SPEXP', 'SPGAU', 'SPLIN', 'SPRAT' and 'SPSPH' and max(2, 2 * estimate) for 'PHYPL' and 'PHYPD'.

None tol float

Convergence tolerance of the root finding (default eps^0.25).

DEFAULT_TOL maxiter int

Maximum number of iterations of the root finding.

1000 eptries int

Number of attempts to find the bounds: when the model cannot be fitted at an end of the interval searched, that end is moved towards the estimate by 1 / eptries of the distance and tried again.

10 verbose bool | int

Print the steps of the root finding on stdout, with digits decimals.

False digits int | None

Number of decimals used for verbose output and the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None control Mapping[str, Any] | None

metafor's list of settings (vc_min, vc_max, tol, maxiter and eptries, written with . or _). Its entries replace the keyword arguments of the same name. Names must be given in full; entries that only other functions of metafor read, including verbose, are ignored here, and any other entry raises InputError.

None xlim Sequence[float] | None

Interval (vc_min, vc_max) searched for the bounds (metafor's ... argument). Wins over control.

None extint bool

Let the search for a bound widen the interval (R's extendInt).

False parm Any

Ignored, with a warning, as in metafor.

None

Returns:

Type Description ConfintResult | ConfintList

A ConfintResult for the requested component and/or the coefficients (fixed=True). With neither given, one result

ConfintResult | ConfintList

per estimated component in a ConfintList (a list, in the order sigma2, tau2, rho, gamma2, phi), or a single result if

ConfintResult | ConfintList

ConfintResult | ConfintList

warning.

more than one component argument is given, the model has no such (estimated) component or it was fixed, the interval searched does not contain the estimate, xlim is not of length 2, control has an unknown entry, or the model has no component to give an interval for.

confint_rma_ls(
    model: RMALSResult,
    *,
    fixed: bool = False,
    alpha: int | None = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    tol: float = DEFAULT_TOL,
    maxiter: int = 1000,
    eptries: int = 10,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    extint: bool = False,
    parm: Any = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> ConfintResult | ConfintList

Confidence intervals for the scale (or location) coefficients of a location-scale model (metafor's confint.rma.ls).

Intervals for the scale coefficients are profile-likelihood intervals. The intervals for the location coefficients (fixed=True) are of Wald type.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMALSResult

Location-scale model fitted by rma_uni with scale.

required fixed bool

Give Wald-type intervals for the location coefficients (t distribution if the test is 't', 'knha' or 'adhoc', else normal). Without alpha only these are returned; with alpha, the interval of the scale coefficient is returned too.

False alpha int | None

0-based position of the scale coefficient to compute the profile-likelihood interval for. Default: all estimated scale coefficients (unless fixed=True).

None level float | None

Confidence level in percent (95 is 95%). As in metafor, a value below 1 is read as the confidence level if it is above 0.5 (0.95) and as the significance level otherwise (0.05). Default: the level of the model.

None transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to each location coefficient and bound (with fixed=True) separately; the bounds are put in order. Default: none.

None targs Any

Second argument passed to transf (transf(value, targs)). Default: none (the integral and mode transformations get no default tau2).

None control Mapping[str, Any] | None

Settings of the root finding: vc_min and vc_max (also written vc.min, vc.max; the interval searched for the bounds), tol, maxiter, eptries and verbose (the entry verbose has no effect, see verbose). Its entries replace the keyword arguments of the same name. Names must be given in full; entries that only other functions of metafor read are ignored and any other entry raises InputError. The default interval searched for the bounds of a coefficient is its estimate plus and minus the smaller of ten times its absolute value and ten times the normal critical value times its standard error (the former only if the standard error is NaN), limited by alpha_min and alpha_max of the control of the fitted model.

None tol float

Convergence tolerance of the root finding (default eps^0.25).

DEFAULT_TOL maxiter int

Maximum number of iterations of the root finding.

1000 eptries int

Number of attempts to find the bounds: when the model cannot be fitted at an end of the interval searched, that end is moved towards the estimate by 1 / eptries of the distance and tried again.

10 xlim Sequence[float] | None

Interval (vc_min, vc_max) searched for the bounds (metafor's ... argument). Wins over control.

None extint bool

Let the search for a bound widen the interval (R's extendInt).

False parm Any

Ignored, with a warning, as in metafor.

None digits int | None

Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None verbose bool

Accepted for compatibility with metafor; it has no effect here (no output is produced).

False

Returns:

Type Description ConfintResult | ConfintList

A ConfintResult with the estimate, ci.lb and ci.ub of the requested coefficient(s); the scale coefficient

ConfintResult | ConfintList

is in the random table (rows alpha.1, alpha.2, ...) and the location coefficients in the fixed table. With no alpha and

ConfintResult | ConfintList

several estimated scale coefficients, a ConfintList (a list of results); a single result if there is one. A bound the search cannot find

ConfintResult | ConfintList

is NaN, with a warning; a bound at the end of the interval searched is shown with a < or > sign.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument is invalid, control has an unknown entry, the model was fitted with optbeta=True, the model has no such (estimated) scale coefficient or no coefficient to give an interval for, or the interval searched does not contain the estimate.

docs.text:
anova_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    model2: RMAResult | None = None,
    *,
    object2: RMAResult | None = None,
    btt: int | Sequence[int] | str | None = None,
    X: ArrayLike | PairmatSpec | None = None,
    rhs: ArrayLike | float | None = None,
    adjust: bool | str | None = None,
    refit: bool = False,
    L: ArrayLike | None = None,
    fixed: bool = False,
    test: str | None = None,
    df: int | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
    abbrev: bool = False,
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    att: Any = None,
    Z: Any = None,
) -> WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

Test coefficients of one rma_uni model, or compare two nested models (metafor's anova.rma).

anova(res, btt=...) tests a subset of coefficients, anova(res, X=L) tests linear combinations L beta = rhs and anova(full, reduced) gives a likelihood-ratio test.

For a model made robust with club_sandwich=True the omnibus test is the cluster-robust Wald test with the small-sample approximation chosen by wald_test of robust (HTZ by default: an F test with df1 and df2 from clubSandwich::Wald_test), and the tests of linear combinations use the degrees of freedom of coef_test. As in R, rhs cannot be used with X for such a model (a warning is given and zero is used).

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/anova.rma.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMAResult

Model fitted by rma_uni.

required model2 RMAResult | None

A second, nested model fitted to the same data, of the same class, for a likelihood-ratio test. The model with more parameters is the full model; when df is given, model is the full model. Default: none, which gives a Wald test of the coefficients of model.

None object2 RMAResult | None

R's name for model2; giving both with different values raises InputError.

None btt int | Sequence[int] | str | None

Coefficients to test jointly: 0-based indices (sorted and without duplicates; an index outside the model raises InputError), a string matched with re.search against the coefficient names (see fixed; metafor uses grep), or a list of several strings or index lists for one test each (a list result, named by the specifications). Default: the coefficients tested by the omnibus test of the model, all but the intercept if there is one.

None X ArrayLike | PairmatSpec | None

Linear combinations of the coefficients to test: a 1-d array (one combination) or a 2-d array with one row per combination, with all p columns or without the intercept column (a column of ones is then added). Each row is tested against rhs; the result holds one test per row and, if X has full row rank, the omnibus test of all of them (QM is otherwise NaN). Also accepted: a pairmat specification. Default: none.

None rhs ArrayLike | float | None

Right-hand side of the hypotheses: a number or one value per combination (or per tested coefficient with btt; a different length raises InputError). Default: 0.

None adjust bool | str | None

Adjust the p-values for multiple testing, as R's p.adjust: True for 'bonferroni', False for 'none', or one of 'holm', 'hochberg', 'hommel', 'bonferroni', 'BH', 'BY', 'fdr' and 'none' (a unique prefix is accepted). It applies to the p-values of the individual tests of the linear combinations, and to the omnibus p-value of a test of moderators (across the elements for a list btt). Default: no adjustment.

None refit bool

For a likelihood-ratio test of REML models whose fixed effects differ, refit them with ML first (otherwise a warning is given).

False L ArrayLike | None

Old spelling of X; if both are given, L is used.

None fixed bool

Match a string btt as a literal substring of the coefficient names instead of as a regular expression.

False test str | None

With model2: 'LRT' (default) for the likelihood-ratio test, or 'Wald' to test the coefficients that only the full model has, with the Wald test of that model (the models must use the same method). A unique prefix is accepted; anything else raises ArgumentError.

None df int | None

With model2: the degrees of freedom of the likelihood-ratio test, instead of the difference in the number of parameters (it is also added to the number of parameters of the full model).

None verbose bool

Add the reason to the error of a cluster-robust test that fails.

False abbrev bool

Remove factor( and ) from the text of the hypotheses of a test of linear combinations (not described on metafor's reference page, but accepted by its source).

False digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

Number of decimals of the printout of the result (also used for the hypotheses of a test of linear combinations), or a mapping as for predict. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None att Any

For location-scale models only; giving it here raises InputError.

None Z Any

For location-scale models only; giving it here raises InputError.

None

Returns:

Type Description WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

For a Wald test, a WaldResult with the omnibus statistic QM, its degrees of freedom QMdf and p-value QMp and,

WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

for linear combinations, the estimates Xb, se, zval, pval and the hypotheses hyp. For two models, an

WaldResult | LRTResult | ListAnovaResult

LRTResult (or, with test='Wald', a WaldResult). For a list btt, a ListAnovaResult (a list of Wald results).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid (for example att or Z is given, X has the wrong number of columns, btt selects nothing, adjust is unknown, the models differ in class or data or in the number of parameters, or a cluster-robust test cannot be computed).

ArgumentError

test is neither 'LRT' nor 'Wald'.

InternalError

an internal invariant does not hold.

Metafor reference

anova.rma

docs.title: hettest
docs.text:
hettest(
    x: RMAResult
    | RMAMVResult
    | FixedBinaryResult
    | RMALSResult
    | SelmodelResult
    | GLMMResult
    | ArrayLike
    | str,
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    *,
    sei: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | None = None,
    data: DataFrame | None = None,
    method: str | None = None,
    test: str | Sequence[str] = 'score',
    boot: bool | int | Sequence[bool] = True,
    progbar: bool = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    mom: bool = False,
    model: RMAResult | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> HettestResult

Test for heteroscedastic heterogeneity in a random-effects model (metafor's hettest).

The standard random-effects model assumes that the heterogeneity of the true effects is homoscedastic; this tests that assumption against study-specific tau^2_i values, with a likelihood-ratio, Wald-type or score test, or with goodness-of-fit tests of the Pearson residuals. P-values come from a parametric bootstrap, the first sample being the data. Without seed the bootstrap uses the generator of set_seed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult | ArrayLike | str

Effect size estimates (an array, or a column name of data), or a random-effects model without moderators (rma_uni), normally fitted by ML or REML. For a model fitted with another method a warning is given and the test is based on method. Models with moderators and other classes of model raise an error.

required vi ArrayLike | str | None

Sampling variances (array or column name). Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model.

None sei ArrayLike | str | None

Standard errors, instead of vi (array or column name). Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model.

None subset ArrayLike | None

Which studies to use: a boolean array or 0-based indices. Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model.

None data DataFrame | None

Data frame holding the variables named in x, vi and sei.

None method str | None

'REML' (default) or 'ML' (case-sensitive; anything else raises InputError). Ignored (with a warning) if x is a model fitted by ML or REML, whose own method is used.

None test str | Sequence[str]

One test or a sequence of tests (case insensitive): 'score' (default), 'lrt' (likelihood ratio), 'wald', or the goodness-of-fit tests of the Pearson residuals 'ksn', 'ksx2', 'adn' and 'adx2' (Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Anderson-Darling tests of normality and of the chi-square distribution of the squared residuals). The goodness-of-fit tests always bootstrap.

'score' boot bool | int | Sequence[bool]

True bootstraps with 1000 samples, a number sets the number of samples (and bootstraps every test), False uses the chi-square approximation with k - 1 degrees of freedom. May be a sequence of bools, one per test (or one for all). The goodness-of-fit tests always bootstrap.

True progbar bool

Print a progress bar to stderr during the bootstrap. Unlike metafor, off by default.

False digits int | None

Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model x (4 for a vector).

None control Mapping[str, Any] | None

Mapping of control values (names written with . or _): tau2i_init (starting values of the tau^2_i: one value or one per study, not negative; default: the tau^2 of the null model, but at least 0.01), threshold (convergence threshold, 1e-8) and maxiter (1000). Not used if x is a model, as in metafor. Names must be given in full (metafor accepts partial names).

None seed int | None

Seed for the bootstrap: it re-seeds the generator of set_seed, as set.seed(seed) does in R, before the samples are drawn. Default: continue with that generator.

None mom bool

Estimate the tau^2_i by the method of moments (max(0, e_i^2 / (1 - h_i) - v_i)).

False model RMAResult | None

For a vector x: an intercept-only model already fitted to the same data, used as the null model instead of fitting it again (metafor's undocumented argument).

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

As R's na.action: studies with missing values in a vector x are omitted with a warning ('omit', 'exclude' and 'pass' act alike), except for 'fail', which raises. No effect for a fitted model.

'omit' verbose bool

Read by metafor but without effect there as well; no effect here.

False

Returns:

Type Description HettestResult

A HettestResult with one entry per requested test in statistic, df, pval, test and boot, plus

HettestResult

tau2i, se_tau2i (Wald-type test) and the bootstrapped statistics statistic_boot.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid (unknown test, method or control entry, wrong length of boot or tau2i_init, k <= 1, a model with moderators), the null model or the tau^2_i could not be estimated, or studies are missing and na_action='fail'.

NotSupportedError

x is a model of a class the test is not available for.

Metafor reference

docs.text:
permutest_rma_uni(
    x: RMAResult,
    exact: bool | Literal['i'] = False,
    iter: int = 1000,
    btt: int | Sequence[int] | str | None = None,
    permci: bool | Sequence[int] = False,
    digits: int | None = None,
    control: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    seed: int | None = None,
    tol: float | None = None,
    fixed: bool = False,
    progbar: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> PermutestResult | int | float

Permutation test for an rma_uni fit (metafor's permutest.rma.uni).

For a model without moderators the signs of the estimates are permuted, otherwise the rows of the model matrix. The p-value is the proportion of permutations whose statistic is as extreme as the observed one (the first permutation of an approximate test is the data, which avoids p-values of 0). With few studies the smallest possible p-value can exceed 0.05.

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/permutest.rma.uni.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult

Model fitted by rma_uni (not a robust result).

required exact bool | Literal['i']

True carries out an exact test (all unique permutations; also used if iter exceeds their number); 'i' returns the number of iterations an exact test needs; False (default) uses iter random permutations.

False iter int

Number of random permutations for an approximate test (at least 2).

1000 btt int | Sequence[int] | str | None

Coefficients the omnibus test refers to: 0-based indices or a string searched for (Python re.search) in the coefficient names. Default: that of the model.

None permci bool | Sequence[int]

True, or 0-based coefficient indices, to also find permutation-based confidence interval bounds (slow). A bound that cannot be found is NaN.

False digits int | None

Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None control Mapping[str, Any] | None

Mapping with metafor's control values: comptol (tolerance of the comparisons), tol and maxiter (root finding for permci), alternative ('two.sided', 'less' or 'greater'), p2defn ('abs' or 'px2'), stat ('test' or 'coef'), cialt (alternative for the CI bounds) and distfac (factor widening the search interval for the CI bounds).

None seed int | None

Seed of the random permutations. Default: drawn from the R-compatible generator of set_seed, which is left in the state the permutations ended in, as R's global generator is.

None tol float | None

Old spelling of the comptol entry of control.

None fixed bool

Match a string btt literally instead of as a regular expression.

False progbar bool

Print a progress bar to stderr while the permutations are run (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

False verbose bool

Accepted and ignored (metafor shows the errors of refits that fail during the permutations).

False

Returns:

Type Description PermutestResult | int | float

A PermutestResult with the coefficient table (beta, se, zval, pval, ci_lb, ci_ub), the omnibus

PermutestResult | int | float

test (QM, QMp) and the permutation distributions. With exact='i', the number of iterations an exact test needs.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

iter is below 2; btt or permci names a coefficient that does not exist; a control entry is not accepted; an exact test needs more iterations than the largest float.

ArgumentError

control has an unknown entry.

NotSupportedError

x is a robust result.

ValueError

an exact test needs more iterations than can be allocated (R stops with an error as well).

docs.text:
vif_rma_uni(
    res: RMAResult,
    btt: int
    | str
    | Sequence[int | str | Sequence[int]]
    | None = None,
    att: Any = None,
    table: bool = False,
    reestimate: bool = False,
    sim: bool | int = False,
    progbar: bool = True,
    seed: int | None = None,
    parallel: Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore'] = 'no',
    ncpus: int = 1,
    cl: Executor | None = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    intercept: bool = False,
    fixed: bool = False,
    joinb: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
    LB: bool = False,
    joina: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
) -> VIFResult

(Generalized) variance inflation factors for the coefficients of an rma_uni meta-regression (metafor's vif.rma).

A VIF of a coefficient (or a GVIF of a set of coefficients) shows how much the variance of its estimate is inflated by correlation with the other moderators; the SIF is the corresponding inflation of the standard error.

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/vif.rma.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default res RMAResult

Model fitted by rma_uni with moderators (a robust result is accepted, but not with sim or reestimate).

required btt int | str | Sequence[int | str | Sequence[int]] | None

Sets of location coefficients to compute a (generalized) VIF for, 0-based: an int, a string searched for (Python re.search) in the coefficient names, or a list of ints gives one set (one GVIF); a list with lists or strings among its elements gives one set per element (btt=[1, [2, 3], 4], like metafor's btt=list(2, 3:4, 5)). Default: each coefficient except the intercept gets its own VIF.

None att Any

Must be None: metafor uses it for location-scale models only and so does vif_rma_ls; any other value raises an InputError.

None table bool

Add the VIFs to the coefficient table (table of the result; ignored when btt is given).

False reestimate bool

Refit the model with only the coefficients of each set when computing its (G)VIF.

False sim bool | int

Simulate the distribution of each (G)VIF under independence: True for 1000 iterations or a number of iterations (at least 2). The model is refitted with independently permuted variables of the data (a model given as a formula with data) or columns of the model matrix; the result then has sim and prop (nothing is simulated if every (G)VIF is 1). Iteration l is seeded with seed + l when seed is given, as in metafor, otherwise from the stream of set_seed.

False progbar bool

Print a progress bar to stderr while simulating (sim). Default True, as in metafor.

True seed int | None

Seed for the simulation (sim). Default: the stream of set_seed is continued.

None parallel Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore']

Parallel simulation: 'no' (default), 'snow' or 'multicore'; both use a process pool of ncpus workers ('multicore' forks them where the platform allows). As in metafor, 'no' with ncpus > 1 (or with cl) is 'snow', and 'snow' or 'multicore' with ncpus < 2 and no cl runs serially. Any other value raises an InputError.

'no' ncpus int

Number of worker processes (at least 1).

1 cl Executor | None

Executor to run the iterations on instead of a process pool.

None digits int | None

Number of decimals of the printout. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None intercept bool

Include the intercept among the coefficients (it is left out by default).

False fixed bool

Match a string btt literally instead of as a regular expression.

False joinb Sequence[Any] | None

One label per column of the model matrix; with sim the columns that share a label are permuted together (then the columns of the model matrix are permuted, not the data).

None LB bool

Accepted as in metafor, where it balances the load of a 'snow' cluster; it changes nothing here.

False joina Sequence[Any] | None

Accepted and unused (metafor uses it for location-scale models only).

None

Returns:

Type Description VIFResult

The (G)VIFs, a VIFResult with one VIFEntry per coefficient or set (vif, sif, m), the

VIFResult

optional coefficient table and, with sim, the simulated values sim and the proportions prop.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

the model has no moderators; att is given; sim is a number below 2 or sim or reestimate is used with a robust result; btt is the intercept (without intercept=True), is out of range or matches no coefficient; joinb does not have one label per column of the model matrix; parallel is not an accepted value or ncpus is below 1.

docs.title: robust_rma_uni
docs.text:
robust_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    cluster: Cluster,
    *,
    adjust: bool | str = True,
    club_sandwich: bool | None = None,
    vcov: str | None = None,
    coef_test: str | None = None,
    conf_test: str | None = None,
    wald_test: str | None = None,
    clubSandwich: bool | None = None,
    digits: int | Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> RMAResult

Cluster-robust inference for an rma_uni fit (metafor's robust.rma.uni).

The variance-covariance matrix of the coefficients is replaced by a sandwich estimator that is robust to correlated errors within clusters; tests and confidence intervals use it.

R source: https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/robust.rma.uni.r

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMAResult

Model fitted by rma_uni (also a model that was made robust before).

required cluster Cluster

The clustering variable: the name of a column of the data given to the model, or a vector with one value per row of the original data (before subsetting and removal of missing values; a vector with one value per study used in the fit is also accepted). It must not contain missing values.

required adjust bool | str

Small-sample adjustment of the cluster-robust variance-covariance matrix: True (default; CR1, multiplies by n/(n-p), with n clusters and p coefficients), False (CR0), 'Stata1' (or 'Stata') or 'Stata2'. Not used with club_sandwich.

True club_sandwich bool | None

Use the clubSandwich approach (bias-reduced linearization, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom) for the cluster-robust tests and intervals instead of the plain sandwich estimator. Default: False.

None vcov str | None

With club_sandwich (ignored otherwise; this and the next three take exactly the values listed): the variance estimator, 'CR0', 'CR1', 'CR1p', 'CR1S', 'CR2' or 'CR3'. Default: 'CR2'.

None coef_test str | None

With club_sandwich: the test of the coefficients, 'z', 'naive-t', 'naive-tp', 'Satterthwaite' or 'saddlepoint'. The saddlepoint test gives p-values only; the confidence intervals then use conf_test or Satterthwaite. Default: Satterthwaite.

None conf_test str | None

With club_sandwich: the method for the confidence intervals, as coef_test without 'saddlepoint'. Default: that of coef_test.

None wald_test str | None

With club_sandwich: the omnibus test, 'chi-sq', 'Naive-F', 'Naive-Fp', 'HTA', 'HTB', 'HTZ', 'EDF' or 'EDT'. Default: 'HTZ'.

None clubSandwich bool | None

R's spelling of club_sandwich. Giving both with different values is an error.

None digits int | Mapping[str, int] | None

Number of decimals of the printout of the result. Default: the digits option, else that of the model.

None verbose bool

Accepted and ignored (metafor shows the errors of a failing clubSandwich computation).

False

Returns:

Type Description RMAResult

The model with the cluster-robust variance-covariance matrix, standard errors, tests and confidence intervals, an RMAResult

RMAResult

of the same form as the input (its robust attribute is set; without club_sandwich the tests are t tests with n - p degrees of

RMAResult

freedom).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

cluster cannot be found, has the wrong length or has missing values; adjust, vcov, coef_test, conf_test or wald_test is not an accepted value (including conf_test='saddlepoint'); club_sandwich and clubSandwich differ; without club_sandwich the number of clusters is not larger than the number of coefficients.

Metafor reference

vcov(

Variance-covariance matrices of a fitted model (metafor's vcov).

Which matrix is returned depends on type; for 'obs', 'fitted' and 'resid' the frame has one row and column per study of the subset. A deltamethod or matreg result gives its own variance-covariance matrix (vcov.deltamethod, vcov.matreg).

Which matrix: 'fixed' (default; of the coefficients), 'beta' (of the location coefficients), 'alpha' (of the scale coefficients of a location-scale model), 'delta' (of the selection parameters of a selection model), 'obs' (or 'marginal'; of the observed effects), 'fitted' (of the fitted values) or 'resid' (of the residuals). ) -> ResidualResult

Internally standardised residuals of an rma_uni fit (metafor's rstandard.rma.uni).

With type='marginal' the residuals y - X b are divided by the square roots of the diagonal of (I - H) M (I - H)', where M holds the marginal variances; with type='conditional' the residuals are those from the BLUPs, divided by their conditional standard errors. rstudent_rma_mv(
    model: RMAMVResult,
    digits: int = 4,
    progbar: bool = False,
    cluster: str | ArrayLike | None = None,
    reestimate: bool = True,

Externally standardised (deleted) residuals of an rma.mv fit (metafor's rstudent.rma.mv).

Each observation's residual is computed from the fit without it (without its whole cluster if cluster is given); the variance of the deleted residual is the marginal variance of the deleted observation(s) (computed with the variance components estimated without them) plus the variance of their predicted values from the fit without them. With cluster a ClusterResidualResult is returned, which also holds each cluster's X2 statistic.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMAMVResult

A model fitted by rma_mv; not allowed for a model passed through robust.

required digits int

Number of decimals used when the result is printed (default 4).

4 progbar bool

Print a progress bar to stderr while the refits are made (default False).

False cluster str | ArrayLike | None

Clustering variable: a column name of the data the model was fitted to, or a vector with one value per row of that data (before subsetting and removal of rows with missing values, which are applied to it automatically). Whole clusters are then deleted in turn. None (the default) deletes each observation in turn.

None reestimate bool

Re-estimate the variance and correlation components after each deletion (default True). With False they stay at the full-model values, which is faster and only approximate.

'omit'

influence_rma_uni(
    model: RMAResult,
    digits: int | None = None,
    *,
    btt: int | Sequence[int] | str | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    measure: str = 'all',
    progbar: bool = False,
) -> InfluenceResult | Series | DataFrame | ResidualResult

Leave-one-out diagnostics for an rma.uni fit (metafor's influence()).

The model is refitted without each study in turn, which gives the externally standardised residuals, DFFITS, Cook's distances, covariance ratios, DFBETAS, leave-one-out tau^2 and QE, hat values and weights (Viechtbauer & Cheung, 2010, doi:10.1002/jrsm.11). Studies whose refit fails (or loses a coefficient) get NaN.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model RMAResult

A model fitted by rma_uni; not allowed for a model passed through robust (except with measure='cooks.distance').

required digits int | None

Number of decimals used when the result is printed. None uses the digits option, else the digits of the model.

None btt int | Sequence[int] | str | None

The coefficients Cook's distance and the covariance ratio refer to, as 0-based indices (or a regular expression matched against the coefficient names). None (the default) uses all coefficients.

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

How studies dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; no row for them), 'exclude' or 'pass' (a row of missing values for each, so the result has one row per supplied study) or 'fail' (raise an error).

'omit' measure str

Metafor's undocumented argument that restricts the result: 'cooks.distance' gives only the Cook's distances (as cooks_distance), 'dfbetas' only the DFBETAS (as dfbetas) and 'rstudent' only the deleted residuals (as rstudent). Any other value (the default is 'all') gives the full result.

'all' progbar bool

Print a progress bar to stderr while the studies are left out in turn (default False); no bar is shown with measure='cooks.distance' or 'rstudent'.

False

The inf property is the studies' influence table (columns rstudent, dffits, cook.d, cov.r, tau2.del, QE.del, hat, weight and inf), dfbs the DFBETAS (one column per coefficient) and is_infl marks the studies metafor flags with an asterisk: |DFFITS| > 3 sqrt(p/(k-p)), the lower-tail area of a chi-square distribution with m degrees of freedom cut off by Cook's distance above 50%, hat > 3p/k or any |DFBETAS| > 1.

Refit an intercept-only rma.uni model leaving out each study (or each cluster of studies).

transf is applied to the estimates and CI bounds (the integral and mode transformations default to the model's tau2); the standard errors are then NaN. cluster gives one value per study supplied (or a column name in the data the model was fitted to) and leaves out all studies of one cluster at a time. With na_action='exclude'/'pass' (and no cluster) the output has one row per supplied study.

Parameters:

docs.text:
cumul_rma_uni(
    x: RMAResult,
    order: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    digits: int | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    collapse: bool = False,
    *,
    decreasing: bool = False,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    progbar: bool = False,
) -> CumulResult

Fit the intercept-only model to the first i studies for i = 1, ..., k (metafor's cumul.rma.uni).

A cumulative meta-analysis describes the accumulation of evidence as studies are added, typically in chronological order (Chalmers & Lau, 1993, doi:10.1177/096228029300200204; Lau, Schmid & Chalmers, 1995, doi:10.1016/0895-4356(94)00106-Z). Studies dropped for missing values in the fit are skipped. na_action stands for R's options(na.action=), as in metafor (see https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/cumul.rma.uni.r).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult

A model without moderators (an equal- or random-effects model) fitted by rma_uni; not allowed for a model passed through robust.

required order ArrayLike | str | None

Variable giving the order in which the studies are added, ascending: a column name of the data the model was fitted to, or an array with one value per supplied study. Studies with a missing value are not added. None (the default) uses the original order and ignores collapse.

None digits int | None

Number of decimals used when the result is printed. None uses the digits option, else the digits of the model.

None transf Callable[..., Any] | None

A function applied to the estimates and confidence interval bounds (for example numpy.exp). The integral and mode transformations of metafopy.transf use the tau2 of the model. The standard errors are then NaN. None (the default) applies no transformation.

None targs Any

Extra argument passed to transf as transf(x, targs). None (the default) calls transf(x).

None collapse bool

Add studies with the same value of order together instead of one at a time (default False).

False decreasing bool

Add the studies in descending order of order (default False). metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument.

False na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

How studies dropped for missing values are handled: 'omit' (the default; no row for them), 'exclude' or 'pass' (a row of missing values for each) or 'fail' (raise an error).

'omit' progbar bool

Print a progress bar to stderr while the refits are made (default False).

False

    res: RMAResult,

    targs: Any = None,

BLUPs of the true effects of an rma.uni fit (metafor's blup.rma.uni).

The prediction for study i shrinks its observed effect towards the model's fitted value (the empirical Bayes estimate of its true effect). Prediction intervals use a normal distribution, or a t-distribution with the model's ddf degrees of freedom (k - p unless dfs was given) when the model was fitted with a t, knha or adhoc test. For equal- and fixed-effects models the BLUPs equal the fitted values. na_action plays the role of R's options(na.action=).

gosh_rma_uni(
    x: RMAResult,
    subsets: int | None = None,
    *,
    seed: int | None = None,
    rng: RRandom | None = None,
    progbar: bool = False,
    parallel: Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore'] = 'no',
    ncpus: int = 1,
    cl: Executor | None = None,
    LB: bool = False,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> GoshResult

Fit the model to subsets of the studies (metafor's gosh.rma).

Olkin, Dahabreh & Trikalinos (2012, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1053) proposed examining the pooled estimate and the heterogeneity statistics of the model fitted to all subsets of the studies; Viechtbauer (2021) generalised this to models with moderators. By default all subsets (with at least p studies, p being the number of coefficients) are used if there are at most 10**6 of them, otherwise 10**6 random subsets are drawn. The subsets are drawn before the fits, so the result equals that of a serial run.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult

A model fitted by rma_uni, with or without moderators; not allowed for a model passed through robust, or for location-scale and selection models.

required subsets int | None

Number of subsets to use. None (the default) uses all subsets if there are at most 10**6, else 10**6 random ones. If it is at least the number of possible subsets, all subsets are used. Must be 2 or more.

None seed int | None

Seed of the R-compatible random number generator used to draw random subsets, so that gosh(res, seed=s) draws the same subset sizes and study indices as R's set.seed(s). None uses the global generator (see set_seed). Only used when random subsets are drawn.

None rng RRandom | None

An R-compatible generator to draw the random subsets from, instead of seed or the global generator.

None progbar bool

Print a progress bar (per block of subsets) to stderr (default False; metafor's default is TRUE).

False parallel Literal['no', 'snow', 'multicore']

'no' (the default), 'snow' or 'multicore'; fit the subsets in a process pool (see ncpus).

'no' ncpus int

Number of worker processes (default 1; a value above 1 turns parallel processing on).

1 cl Executor | None

An executor to fit the subsets on, instead of one created for the call.

None LB bool

metafor reads this undocumented extra argument to use load-balanced scheduling with parallel='snow'; accepted here and ignored.

False na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

Stands for R's options(na.action=); metafor only checks that it is one of 'omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail', and so does this function.

'omit'

k, QE, I2, H2, tau2, tau and the coefficient estimates (estimate for a model without moderators);

docs.title: vcalc
docs.text:
vcalc(
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    cluster: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    subgroup: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    obs: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    type: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    time1: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    time2: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    grp1: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    grp2: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    w1: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    w2: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    data: DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    rho: float
    | ArrayLike
    | DataFrame
    | Sequence[Any]
    | None = None,
    phi: float | None = None,
    rvars: Sequence[str | int] | slice | None = None,
    checkpd: bool = True,
    nearpd: bool = False,
    sparse: bool = False,
    retdat: bool = False,
) -> NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

Variance-covariance matrix of dependent estimates, block diagonal over cluster (metafor's vcalc).

Rows with the same cluster (and subgroup) may be dependent, rows of different clusters are independent. Within a cluster the correlation of two estimates is built from rho (estimates of the same or of different constructs), from phi and the time points time1/time2 (an autoregressive structure), and from the groups grp1/grp2 with sizes w1/w2 for estimates that are contrasts between two conditions and so share a condition. The matrix can be used as the V argument of rma_mv. With rvars the correlation matrices of the clusters are read from columns of data instead.

Differences from R: metafor's undocumented nearPD alias of nearpd is not accepted; in rvars mode the matrix of a cluster is placed at that cluster's rows even when the rows of a cluster are not contiguous (R places the blocks in order of first appearance, which misaligns the matrix in that case).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default vi ArrayLike | str | None

Sampling variances of the estimates, as an array or the name of a column of data. Required. A single value is repeated for as many rows as cluster has.

None cluster ArrayLike | str | None

Clustering variable (for example the study), an array or a column name. Required, without missing values. Rows with the same value may be dependent.

None subgroup ArrayLike | str | None

Variable distinguishing independent subgroups within clusters (no overlap of subjects), an array or a column name. Rows of different subgroups are independent even in the same cluster. None for no subgroups.

None obs ArrayLike | str | None

Variable distinguishing different estimates of the same construct or response variable (for example several scales for depression), an array or a column name. Needs rho.

None type ArrayLike | str | None

Variable distinguishing different types of constructs or response variables, an array or a column name. Needs rho.

None time1 ArrayLike | str | None

Numeric time points at which the estimates were obtained (in the first condition for contrasts), an array or a column name. Needs phi.

None time2 ArrayLike | str | None

Numeric time points in the second condition for contrasts between two conditions, an array or a column name.

None grp1 ArrayLike | str | None

Group of the first condition for estimates that are contrasts between two conditions (for example [2, 3] with grp2=[1, 1] for two treatments versus one control), an array or a column name. Give grp1 alone or with grp2.

None grp2 ArrayLike | str | None

Group of the second condition, an array or a column name.

None w1 ArrayLike | str | None

Size of the group of the first condition (or more generally its inverse-sampling-variance weight), numeric, an array or a column name. Default: equal group sizes, which implies a correlation of 0.5 between contrasts that share a condition.

None w2 ArrayLike | str | None

Size (weight) of the group of the second condition, numeric, an array or a column name.

None data DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None

Data frame (or mapping of columns) holding the variables named above.

None rho float | ArrayLike | DataFrame | Sequence[Any] | None

Correlation of the sampling errors of estimates measured concurrently. A scalar, or a correlation matrix as a data frame whose row and column labels are the unique values of obs (or of type). With both obs and type a pair: the first element (a scalar or matrix) is the within-construct correlation among the obs values, the second the between-construct correlation among the type values.

None phi float | None

Autocorrelation of the sampling errors of two estimates that differ by one unit of time1.

None rvars Sequence[str | int] | slice | None

Columns of data that hold the correlation matrices of the clusters: names or 0-based positions, or a slice of names (slice('r1', 'r4') for R's r1:r4). The first k_i columns hold the lower triangle of the matrix of the i-th cluster (k_i rows); there must be as many columns as the largest cluster has rows. When given, all variable arguments except vi, cluster and subgroup are ignored. Needs data.

None checkpd bool

Warn about clusters whose variance-covariance matrix is not positive definite (default True).

True nearpd bool

Replace such matrices by the nearest correlation matrix (Matrix::nearPD(corr=TRUE) in R). Use with care (default False).

False sparse bool

Return a sparse matrix (default False).

False retdat bool

Return a data frame of the variables used with the matrix appended in columns V.1, V.2, ... instead of the matrix (default False; metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument).

False

Returns:

Type Description NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

The k x k variance-covariance matrix, with k the length of vi: a dense array that prints like metafor's vcovmat

NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

(VCovMat), a scipy.sparse.csr_array if sparse=True, or with retdat=True a data frame of

NDArray[float64] | csr_array | DataFrame

the variables used with the matrix in the columns V.1, V.2, ....

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument or the data is invalid (R stops with an error here).

NotFoundError

a named column is not in data.

ArgumentError

rho has an unsupported type.

Metafor reference

docs.title: rcalc
docs.text:
rcalc(
    x: str
    | (NDArray[float64] | DataFrame)
    | Sequence[NDArray[float64] | DataFrame]
    | Mapping[str, NDArray[float64] | DataFrame],
    ni: ArrayLike | str | None | float = None,
    data: DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    rtoz: bool = False,
    nfun: str | Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float] = 'min',
    sparse: bool = False,
    upper: bool = False,
    simplify: bool = True,
    *,
    rowid: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    vnames: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    noid: bool | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

Variance-covariance matrix of correlation coefficients from the same samples (metafor's rcalc).

Correlations computed from the same sample are not independent. Equations for the sampling covariances can be found in Steiger (1980, doi:10.1037/0033-2909.87.2.245) and Olkin and Finn (1990, doi:10.1037/0033-2909.108.2.330); for raw correlations the denominator is ni - 1 (as in metafor), for r-to-z transformed ones ni - 3. The data and the matrix can be passed on to rma_mv. As in R, the study identifier in dat consists of strings (the names of the list, or the ids converted to character).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x str | (NDArray[float64] | DataFrame) | Sequence[NDArray[float64] | DataFrame] | Mapping[str, NDArray[float64] | DataFrame]

A formula string such as 'ri ~ var1 + var2 | study' (the study part may be left out for a single study), naming the correlations, the two variables of each and the study in data; or a correlation matrix; or a list or dict of correlation matrices. Matrices are arrays or data frames whose column labels name the variables (x1, x2, ... if unnamed).

required ni ArrayLike | str | None | float

Sample sizes the correlations are based on: for a formula, a column name of data or an array; for a matrix, the (common) sample size; for a list of matrices, one sample size per matrix. Required.

None data DataFrame | Mapping[str, Any] | None

Data frame (or mapping of columns) holding the variables of the formula (and ni). Required for a formula.

None rtoz bool

Transform the correlations with Fisher's r-to-z transformation and compute the matrix for the transformed values (default False).

False nfun str | Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]

How the common sample size within a study is computed when it differs between correlations: 'min' (the default; conservative), 'harmonic' (harmonic mean) or 'mean', an unambiguous prefix of these, or a function of the array of the sample sizes of a study returning a single value.

'min' sparse bool

Return the matrix as a sparse matrix (default False; only with a list of matrices or a formula does this give a sparse V).

False upper bool

For matrices, use the upper instead of the lower triangle (default False; metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument).

False simplify bool

For a list of matrices, combine the results into one (default True); with False a dict of one result per matrix (metafor takes this as an undocumented extra argument).

True rowid Sequence[str] | None

For a list of matrices with simplify=True: values of 'id.var1.var2' giving the order of the rows of dat and V (metafor passes this on internally for a formula).

None vnames Sequence[str] | None

For a list of matrices with simplify=True: four names for the columns of dat.

None noid bool | None

For a list of matrices with simplify=True: drop the study identifier from dat (default False).

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

Stands for R's options(na.action=); an unknown value raises, the known ones ('omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' and 'fail') give the same result (metafor sets na.pass while it computes).

'omit'

Returns:

Type Description RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

An RCalcResult with the data dat (one row per correlation) and the block diagonal variance-covariance matrix

RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

V. A covariance is NaN when a correlation it needs is missing, and nothing is computed for studies with a common sample size

RCalcResult | dict[str, RCalcResult]

below 5. With simplify=False and a list of matrices, a dict of one such result per matrix.

Raises:

Type Description ArgumentError

x is not a formula, a matrix or a list of matrices.

InputError

an argument or the data is invalid (R stops with an error here).

NotFoundError

a variable of the formula is not in data.

docs.title: Regression on correlation and covariance matrices
matreg
docs.text:
matreg(
    y: int | str,
    x: Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None = None,
    R: ArrayLike | DataFrame | None = None,
    n: float | None = None,
    V: ArrayLike | DataFrame | None = None,
    cov: bool = False,
    means: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ztor: bool = False,
    nearpd: bool = False,
    level: float = 95,
    digits: int | None = None,
) -> MatregResult

Fit a regression model to a correlation or covariance matrix (metafor's matreg).

y is the outcome: a 0-based index into R, a variable name (R must then be a frame with dimension names) or a formula string such as 'perf ~ acog + asom + conf' (which also gives x). x are the predictors (indices or names; by default every other variable). Give either n, the sample size the matrix is based on, or V, the variance-covariance matrix of the elements of the lower triangle of R (column-wise, with the diagonal when cov=True), for instance from :func:metafopy.rcalc or the vcov() of a multivariate model of correlations. cov=True treats R as a covariance matrix (the model then has an intercept, which needs means), ztor=True back-transforms Fisher r-to-z transformed correlations (and their V) and nearpd=True replaces a non-positive-definite R[x, x] by the nearest correlation matrix (:func:metafopy.core.linalg.near_pd, a port of Matrix::nearPD).

Without names, the coefficients are labelled x1, x2, ... by their 1-based position in R, as in R.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default y int | str

The outcome variable: a 0-based index into R, a variable name (R must then be a data frame with dimension names) or a formula string such as 'perf ~ acog + asom + conf', which also gives x.

required x Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None

The predictor variables: a sequence of 0-based indices or names (or a single one). Ignored when y is a formula. None (the default) uses every variable other than y.

None R ArrayLike | DataFrame | None

The correlation or covariance matrix (an array or data frame; required). Only its lower triangle (including the diagonal) is used.

None n float | None

The sample size the matrix is based on; gives the standard errors of a regression on raw data (t tests). Give n or V, not both.

None V ArrayLike | DataFrame | None

The variance-covariance matrix of the elements of the lower triangle of R, column-wise (with the diagonal when cov=True), for instance from rcalc or the vcov() of a multivariate model of correlations. Gives the standard errors by the multivariate delta method (z tests). Give n or V, not both.

None cov bool

Treat R as a covariance matrix; the model then has an intercept, which needs means (default False, a correlation matrix).

False means ArrayLike | None

The means of the variables, for the intercept when cov=True. Without them the intercept estimate is NaN.

None ztor bool

R (and V) hold Fisher r-to-z transformed correlations, which are back-transformed to raw correlations first (default False).

False nearpd bool

Replace an R[x, x] that cannot be inverted (is not positive definite) by the nearest correlation matrix (a port of Matrix::nearPD) instead of failing (default False). Treat the results with caution. metafor's undocumented nearPD alias of this argument is not accepted.

False level float

Confidence interval level in percent (default 95), or a value below 1 read as in metafor.

95 digits int | None

Number of decimals used when the result is printed (default 4).

None

Returns:

Type Description MatregResult

A MatregResult: the table tab of (standardised, for a correlation matrix) regression coefficients with

MatregResult

their standard errors, test statistics, p-values and confidence interval bounds, the variance-covariance matrix vb of the

MatregResult

coefficients, R2 and further fit statistics. It has coef, vcov, confint and predict methods.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

an argument is missing, invalid or inconsistent with R.

ArgumentError

a logical argument is not a bool.

EstimationError

R[x, x] cannot be inverted, or n does not exceed the number of regression coefficients.

Metafor reference

docs.title: emmprep
docs.text:
emmprep(
    x: RMAResult
    | RMAMVResult
    | GLMMResult
    | FixedBinaryResult
    | RMALSResult
    | SelmodelResult,
    verbose: bool = False,
    *,
    data: DataFrame | None = None,
    df: float | None = None,
    sigma: float | None = None,
    tran: Link | str | None = None,
    at: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    cov_reduce: Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]
    | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]]
    | None = None,
    nesting: str
    | Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]]
    | None
    | Literal['auto'] = 'auto',
) -> EmmGrid

Prepare a reference grid from a fitted model, as metafor's emmprep does for emmeans' qdrg.

The grid has one row per combination of the levels of the factors in the model formula, with each numeric predictor at its mean over the studies (cov_reduce) or at the values given in at. Pass the grid to emmeans (and then to contrast, pairs and regrid) to get estimated marginal means. When the model knows its effect size measure, the back-transformation (for example exponentiation for log ratios) is stored in the grid and applied by type='response'.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | GLMMResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult

A fitted model with a formula: a model from rma_uni, rma_mv, rma_glmm, rma_mh or rma_peto, a location-scale model or a selection model. Models with redundant predictors that were dropped cannot be used.

required verbose bool

Print the extracted formula, degrees of freedom, tau^2 and transformation (default False).

False data DataFrame | None

Data frame with the variables of the model, to build the grid from instead of the data used in the fit. None (the default) uses the data of the fit.

None df float | None

Degrees of freedom of the tests and intervals. None (the default) takes them from the fit (the smallest ddf; infinite for z tests).

None sigma float | None

Error standard deviation used for bias adjustment in back-transformations (the square root of tau^2). None (the default) takes it from the fit, or 0 for rma_mv and location-scale fits, where it cannot be extracted.

None tran Link | str | None

Transformation of the estimates, a link object or its name (for example 'log' or 'logit'), or 'none' for none. As in emmeans, a name that is no known transformation gives the identity link carrying that name; '+.sqrt' is not supported. None (the default) derives it from the effect size measure ('log' for ratio measures, 'logit' for PLO, and so on).

None at Mapping[str, Any] | None

Mapping from variable names to the values to use in the grid: for a numeric predictor its values instead of its mean, for a factor a subset of its levels. Other variables are as by default.

None cov_reduce Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float] | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]] | None

Function reducing the values of a numeric predictor to the one used in the grid, or a mapping from variable names to such functions. None (the default) uses the mean.

None nesting str | Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]] | None | Literal['auto']

Factors nested in others, as text such as 'grp %in% lat' (several separated by commas) or a mapping from each nested factor to the factor(s) it is nested in. 'auto' (the default) detects the nesting from the combinations of levels in the data and the terms of the model (lat + lat:grp nests grp in lat); None switches the detection off. Combinations that cannot occur are hidden and left out of the means.

'auto'

Returns:

Type Description EmmGrid

An EmmGrid: the reference grid, with the coefficients and their variance-covariance matrix, the degrees of freedom

EmmGrid

and the transformation stored.

Raises:

Type Description ArgumentError

x is not a fitted model of a supported class.

InputError

the fit cannot be used (redundant predictors, no formula or data) or an argument is invalid.

NotSupportedError

tran is '+.sqrt'.

Metafor reference

emmprep

docs.title: emmeans
docs.text:
emmeans(
    object: EmmGrid
    | (
        RMAResult
        | RMAMVResult
        | GLMMResult
        | FixedBinaryResult
        | RMALSResult
        | SelmodelResult
    ),
    specs: str | Sequence[str],
    by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    *,
    weights: str
    | Sequence[float]
    | Sequence[Sequence[float]]
    | NDArray[float64] = 'equal',
    at: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    cov_reduce: Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]
    | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]]
    | None = None,
    null: float | None = None,
    delta: float | None = None,
    side: int | float | str | None = None,
    type: str | None = None,
    **prep: Any,
) -> EmmGrid

Estimated marginal means: the reference grid averaged over the variables not named in specs (and by).

object is a reference grid from :func:emmprep or a fit (at, cov_reduce and further keywords then go to :func:emmprep). specs names the variables ('alloc', ['alloc', 'lat'] or an R-style '~ alloc | lat'; '1' or '~ 1' for the overall mean) and by the variables the results are grouped by. weights averages over the other factors with 'equal' weights, 'proportional' (frequencies in the data), 'outer' (products of the marginal frequencies), 'cells' or 'flat' (cell frequencies, the latter ignoring empty cells), a vector with one weight per combination of those factors, or a matrix whose columns are those combinations and whose rows are the weights of the successive means (recycled when there are more means than rows).

With nested factors (see :func:emmprep) the means of a nested factor are given within the groups it is nested in, and the other factors are averaged over the combinations that occur in the data. null, delta and side set the defaults of the tests of :meth:EmmGrid.summary; so does type ('response' shows the back-transformed means by default, as emmeans(..., type='response')). See https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/reference/emmeans.html.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default object EmmGrid | (RMAResult | RMAMVResult | GLMMResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult)

A reference grid from emmprep, or a fitted model (see emmprep for the classes), for which a grid is made first.

required specs str | Sequence[str]

The variables to get means for: a name, a sequence of names, or an R-style formula such as '~ alloc | lat'; '1' or '~ 1' for the overall mean.

required by str | Sequence[str] | None

Variables the results are grouped by. None (the default) for none (or those after | in specs).

None weights str | Sequence[float] | Sequence[Sequence[float]] | NDArray[float64]

How the other factors are averaged over (a string may be abbreviated, for example 'prop'): 'equal' (the default), 'proportional' (frequencies in the data), 'outer' (products of the marginal frequencies), 'cells' or 'flat' (cell frequencies, the latter ignoring empty cells), a vector with one weight per combination of those factors, or a matrix whose columns are those combinations and whose rows are the weights of the successive means (recycled when there are more means than rows).

'equal' at Mapping[str, Any] | None

Mapping from variable names to the values of the grid (see emmprep); only when object is a fitted model.

None cov_reduce Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float] | Mapping[str, Callable[[NDArray[float64]], float]] | None

Reduction of the numeric predictors (see emmprep); only when object is a fitted model.

None null float | None

Value the tests of the summary compare the estimates with. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

None delta float | None

Threshold of equivalence and non-inferiority tests of the summary. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

None side int | float | str | None

Tail of the tests of the summary: -1, 0 or 1 (or '<', '!=', '>', or a word such as 'left', 'both', 'right', 'noninferiority', 'equivalence'). None keeps the value of the grid (default both sides).

None type str | None

Default scale of summaries: 'link' (the transformed scale) or 'response' (back-transformed). None (the default) keeps the default of the grid.

None **prep Any

Further keywords for emmprep (verbose, data, df, sigma, tran, nesting); only when object is a fitted model.

{}

Returns:

Type Description EmmGrid

An EmmGrid of the estimated marginal means (with summary() to get the table).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

a variable is not in the grid, the weights do not fit the averaged factors, type is not 'link' or 'response', or at, cov_reduce or other emmprep keywords are given with a reference grid.

docs.title: contrast
docs.text:
contrast(
    object: EmmGrid,
    method: str | Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] = 'eff',
    *,
    by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    interaction: bool | str | Sequence[str] = False,
    name: str = 'contrast',
    adjust: str | None = None,
    ref: int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None = None,
    exclude: int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None = None,
    include: int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None = None,
    reverse: bool = False,
    wts: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    max_degree: int | None = None,
    enhance_levels: bool = True,
    null: float | None = None,
    delta: float | None = None,
    side: int | float | str | None = None,
) -> EmmGrid

Contrasts of the estimates of a reference grid or of marginal means (emmeans' contrast).

method is one of :data:metafopy.methods.emm_contrasts.METHODS ('pairwise', 'revpairwise', 'trt_vs_ctrl', 'trt_vs_ctrlk', 'dunnett', 'eff', 'del_eff', 'consec', 'mean_chg', 'poly', 'identity') or a mapping from contrast names to coefficient vectors, one per row of the grid. The contrasts are formed separately for each combination of the by variables (those of object by default). ref, exclude and include are 0-based indices or level labels. With interaction (True for method on every factor, or one method per factor) contrasts of contrasts are formed, one per combination of the factors. null, delta and side set the defaults of the tests of :meth:EmmGrid.summary.

With nested factors the contrasts are formed within each combination of the groups in by (those a nested factor is nested in are added to it), and the groups can differ in size; only the named methods can be used then. See https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/reference/contrast.html.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default object EmmGrid

A reference grid or marginal means (EmmGrid).

required method str | Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]

The contrasts: the name of a method ('pairwise', 'revpairwise', 'tukey', 'trt_vs_ctrl', 'trt_vs_ctrl1', 'trt_vs_ctrlk', 'dunnett', 'eff' (the default), 'del_eff', 'consec', 'mean_chg', 'poly' or 'identity'), or a mapping from contrast names to coefficient vectors with one value per row of the grid (per group).

'eff' by str | Sequence[str] | None

Variables to form the contrasts within. None (the default) uses those of object.

None interaction bool | str | Sequence[str]

False (the default) for ordinary contrasts. True forms contrasts of contrasts, applying method to every factor, and a name or sequence of names gives the method for each factor; one contrast per combination of the factors results.

False name str

Name of the column of the contrasts (default 'contrast').

'contrast' adjust str | None

Multiplicity adjustment stored in the result for its tests and intervals: 'tukey', 'scheffe', 'sidak', 'dunnettx', 'mvt', 'holm', 'hochberg', 'hommel', 'bonferroni', 'BH', 'BY', 'fdr' or 'none'. None (the default) uses the default of the method (for example 'tukey' for 'pairwise'). As in emmeans, 'tukey', 'scheffe' and 'dunnettx' apply to two-sided tests only, and the methods of p.adjust ('holm' to 'fdr') to tests, not intervals (which then use 'bonferroni').

None ref int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None

The reference level(s) of 'trt_vs_ctrl' and similar methods: 0-based indices or level labels. Default the first level.

None exclude int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None

Levels left out of the contrasts: 0-based indices or level labels.

None include int | str | Sequence[int | str] | None

Levels to use in the contrasts (the others are left out): 0-based indices or level labels.

None reverse bool

Reverse the direction of the contrasts, for example later minus earlier (default False).

False wts Sequence[float] | None

Weights of the levels for the 'eff' and 'del_eff' methods, normalised to sum to 1: one value per level, or per included level when exclude or include is used. None (the default) for equal weights. emmeans' wts = NA (take the weights from the grid) is not supported.

None max_degree int | None

Maximum degree of the 'poly' contrasts (at most 20). None (the default) for min(6, k - 1) with k levels, as the max.degree default of emmeans' poly.emmc.

None enhance_levels bool

Put the variable name in front of numeric levels in the labels of the contrasts (default True).

True null float | None

Value the tests of the summary compare the estimates with. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

None delta float | None

Threshold of equivalence and non-inferiority tests of the summary. None keeps the value of the grid (default 0).

None side int | float | str | None

Tail of the tests of the summary: -1, 0 or 1 (or '<', '!=', '>', or a word such as 'left', 'both', 'right', 'noninferiority', 'equivalence'). None keeps the value of the grid (default both sides).

None

Returns:

Type Description EmmGrid

An EmmGrid of the contrasts, with one row per contrast.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

the method or an argument does not fit the grid.
