docs.text:
plot_profile(
    x: ProfileResult
    | LSProfileResult
    | Sequence[ProfileResult | LSProfileResult],
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    pch: int = 19,
    xlab: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    ylab: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    main: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    refline: bool = True,
    cline: bool | float = False,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    log: str | None = None,
    cex: float = 1.0,
    lwd: float = 1.0,
) -> Axes | list[Axes]

Plot the profile (log-)likelihood computed by profile (plot.profile.rma).

Mirrors metafor's plot.profile.rma(), which is documented with profile.rma.

refline marks the estimate and its (log-)likelihood with dotted lines, cline (True for a significance level of 0.05, or a number as for metafor's level arguments) adds a horizontal line at the likelihood-ratio test's critical value. The estimate itself is added to the profile if it lies within the range of the grid. Returns the axes.

x may also be the list of profiles that profile returns for models with several variance components (rma_mv, location-scale and selection models): one panel per component is drawn in a grid, as par(mfrow = n2mfrow(comps)) makes it (inside ax if given), and the list of axes is returned. xlab, ylab and main are then one string for all panels or one per panel. Unlike metafor, refline also applies to the panels of a list. log ('x', 'y' or 'xy') draws logarithmic axes, cex is the size of the points and lwd the width of the line, which metafor passes on through ....

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x ProfileResult | LSProfileResult | Sequence[ProfileResult | LSProfileResult]

A profile from profile, or the list of profiles it returns for models with several variance components (rma_mv, location-scale and selection models; one panel per component).

required xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis as (low, high). Default: those stored in the profile (x.xlim).

None ylim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high). Default: those stored in the profile (x.ylim).

None pch int

Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code). Default: 19.

19 xlab str | Sequence[str] | None

Label of the horizontal axis; for a list of profiles one string for all panels or one per panel. Default: derived from the profiled component (for example tau^2 Value).

None ylab str | Sequence[str] | None

Label of the vertical axis; for a list of profiles one string for all panels or one per panel. Default: 'Log-Likelihood' (or 'Likelihood' if the profile was computed with exp), preceded by 'Restricted ' for REML.

None main str | Sequence[str] | None

Title; for a list of profiles one string for all panels or one per panel. Default: 'Profile Plot for' and the component.

None refline bool

Mark the estimate and its (log-)likelihood with dotted lines (unlike metafor, also applies to the panels of a list). Default: True.

True cline bool | float

Add a horizontal dotted line at the critical value of the likelihood-ratio test: True for a significance level of 0.05, or a number read as metafor's level is (95 or 0.95 for 95 percent, 0.05 for a significance level of 5 percent). Default: False.

False ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to draw into (for a list of profiles, the area the panels fill). Default: the current axes.

None log str | None

Logarithmic axes: 'x', 'y' or 'xy'. Default: linear axes.

None cex float

Size of the points relative to the default. Default: 1.

1.0 lwd float

Width of the line. Default: 1.

1.0

Returns:

Type Description Axes | list[Axes]

The axes drawn into (a list of axes, one per component, for a list of profiles).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

xlab, ylab or main does not have one entry per profile (or is not a single string for a single profile), a limit of a logarithmic axis is not positive, or cline is outside 0 to 100.

Metafor reference

profile.rma

docs.title: plot_gosh
docs.text:
plot_gosh(
    x: GoshResult,
    het: str = 'I2',
    pch: int = 16,
    cex: float | None = None,
    out: int | None = None,
    col: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    alpha: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    border: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    xhist: bool = True,
    yhist: bool = True,
    hh: float | Sequence[float] = 0.3,
    breaks: Any = None,
    adjust: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    labels: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    trim: float
    | Sequence[float | Sequence[float]]
    | None = None,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
) -> PlotGoshResult

Plot the results of gosh (plot.gosh.rma).

Mirrors metafor's plot.gosh.rma().

For a model without moderators the heterogeneity statistic het ('QE', 'I2', 'H2', 'tau2' or 'tau') is plotted against the estimate, with marginal histograms and kernel density estimates (xhist, yhist; hh the relative sizes of the marginal plots, breaks, adjust and lwd their settings, each a single value or a pair for the two margins); with moderators a scatterplot matrix of het and the coefficients is drawn. out (0-based) highlights the subsets that do (col[0]) or do not include that study, alpha gives the transparency of the points, histogram and density line, trim removes the most extreme subsets (a proportion or a list of proportions per column). The panels fill the area of ax.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x GoshResult

The result of gosh.

required het str

Heterogeneity statistic to plot: 'QE', 'I2' (the default), 'H2', 'tau2' or 'tau' ('I^2', 'H^2' and 'tau^2' are accepted too). 'tau2' and 'tau' are not available for equal-effects models.

'I2' pch int

Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code). Default: 16, a filled circle without border.

16 cex float | None

Expansion factor of the points. Default: 0.5.

None out int | None

0-based index of a study to highlight (metafor's out counts from 1): the subsets that include it are drawn in col[0], those without in col[1]. Default: no highlighting.

None col str | Sequence[str] | None

Colour of the points. Default: black. With out it must be two colours (subsets with the out study, subsets without it), default ('red', 'blue').

None alpha float | Sequence[float] | None

Transparency (0 transparent to 1 opaque) of the points, of the histogram bars and of the density lines: one value for the points (the histograms then get 0.5 and the density lines 0.9), two for points and histograms, or all three. Default: n ** -0.2 for n subsets.

None border str | Sequence[str] | None

Border colour of the histogram bars, one for both or a pair (horizontal, vertical margin). Default: light grey. (metafor's FALSE, which omits the borders, is not supported.)

None xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis as (low, high); models without moderators only. Default: the range of the histogram breaks of the estimates.

None ylim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high); models without moderators only. Default: the range of the histogram breaks of het.

None xhist bool

Draw the marginal histogram and density of the estimates; models without moderators only. Default: True.

True yhist bool

Draw the marginal histogram and density of the heterogeneity statistic; models without moderators only. Default: True.

True hh float | Sequence[float]

Relative size of the marginal plots, between 0 and 1 (checked for models without moderators); a single value or a pair for the two margins. For models with moderators it stretches the height of the histograms on the diagonal. Default: 0.3.

0.3 breaks Any

Histogram breaks of the marginal plots, as for R's hist; a single value or a pair. Default: 'Sturges'.

None adjust float | Sequence[float] | None

Bandwidth adjustment of the kernel density estimates (larger is smoother); a single value or a pair. Default: 1.

None lwd float | Sequence[float] | None

Width of the density lines, 0 omits them; a single value or a pair. Default: 2.

None labels Sequence[str] | None

The labels of the horizontal and vertical axes (no moderators) or the names of the variables of the scatterplot matrix. Default: derived from the effect size measure, het and the coefficient names.

None trim float | Sequence[float | Sequence[float]] | None

Remove the most extreme subsets before plotting (an undocumented argument of metafor, passed through ...): the proportion to cut from each tail of every variable (het and the coefficients), or a list with one proportion, or a (lower, upper) pair, per variable.

None ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes whose area the panels fill. Default: the current axes.

None

Returns:

Type Description PlotGoshResult

A PlotGoshResult: for a model without moderators main is the scatterplot and xhist and yhist the marginal histograms (None if

PlotGoshResult

not drawn); for a scatterplot matrix main, xhist and yhist are None and panels holds the axes row by row. axes lists

PlotGoshResult

whichever were drawn.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

het is unknown or 'tau2'/'tau' is used for an equal-effects model, out is not a study, col does not have two colours when out is used, or hh is outside 0 to 1.

Metafor reference

plot.gosh.rma

docs.title: plot_selmodel
docs.text:
plot_selmodel(
    x: SelmodelResult,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    n: int = 1000,
    prec: str | float = 'max',
    scale: bool = False,
    ci: bool | str = False,
    reps: int = 1000,
    shade: bool | str = True,
    rug: bool = True,
    add: bool = False,
    lty: str | int | Sequence[str | int] = LINE_STYLES,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] = (2.0, 1.0),
    seed: int | None = None,
    draw: bool = True,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    bty: str = 'o',
    col: str | None = None,
) -> SelPlotResult

Draw the selection function of a selection model against the p-value.

Mirrors metafor's plot.rma.uni.selmodel().

prec fixes the precision at which the function is drawn ('min', 'max', 'mean', 'median' or a number). ci adds a confidence region: 'wald' transforms the Wald bounds of the selection parameters, 'boot' (or True) simulates reps parameter vectors from their estimated multivariate normal distribution (with NumPy's generator seeded by seed, so the bounds agree with metafor only up to simulation error). scale rescales the curve to the unit interval, shade fills the region, rug marks the observed p-values and add draws into existing axes. draw=False only computes the curve. bty (the type of box around the plot) and col (the colour of the lines) are passed on to plot() and lines() by metafor. The curve is returned as SelPlotResult.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x SelmodelResult

A selection model from selmodel.

required xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis (the p-values for which the function is drawn), within 0 and 1. Default: the model's smallest p-value pval_min to 1 - pval_min, which is 0 to 1 unless the selection function or the pval.min control of selmodel sets a small positive minimum (1e-5 for some functions).

None ylim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high). Default: 0 to 1 for the bounded selection functions (halfnorm, halfnorm2, logistic, logistic2, negexp, negexp2, negexppow, power, power2), otherwise the range of the curve (and of the confidence region).

None n int

Number of p-values within xlim at which the function is computed. Default: 1000. For step functions the step points are added.

1000 prec str | float

Precision at which a selection function that involves one is drawn: 'min' (the most precise study), 'max' (the default, the least precise study), 'mean', 'median' or a number (1 corresponds to 'max', smaller values to higher precision; the number is replaced by 1 if the model was fitted without the prec argument of selmodel).

'max' scale bool

Rescale the curve (and region) to the 0 to 1 range. Default: False.

False ci bool | str

Add a confidence region around the curve: False (the default), True or 'boot' (parametric bootstrap: reps parameter vectors are simulated from the estimated multivariate normal distribution of the selection parameters, with NumPy's generator, so the bounds agree with metafor only up to simulation error), or 'wald' (the curve at the Wald bounds of the parameter; for models with a single selection parameter and for step functions). Nothing is drawn if the model has no standard errors for the parameters.

False reps int

Number of simulated parameter vectors for the 'boot' region. Default: 1000.

1000 shade bool | str

Shade the confidence region: True (the default, light grey), False or a colour.

True rug bool

Mark the observed p-values along the horizontal axis (not with add). Default: True.

True add bool

Add the curve to the existing axes without drawing a new frame, labels or rug. Default: False.

False lty str | int | Sequence[str | int]

Line types of the selection function and of the confidence region bounds, as a pair (a single value serves the curve and the bounds get 'dotted'). Default: ('solid', 'dotted'). Accepts R names ('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash', 'twodash', 'blank'), R codes 0 to 6 or a matplotlib line style.

LINE_STYLES lwd float | Sequence[float]

Line widths of the selection function and of the confidence region bounds, as a pair (a single value serves the curve and the bounds get 1). Default: (2, 1).

(2.0, 1.0) seed int | None

Seed of NumPy's generator for the 'boot' region (not R's generator). Default: not seeded.

None draw bool

If False only compute the curve and do not draw (the returned ax is None). Default: True.

True ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

None bty str

Type of box around the plot: 'o' (the default), 'l', '7', 'c', 'u', ']' or 'n' (none). Ignored with add.

'o' col str | None

Colour of the curve and of the confidence region bounds (the shading has its own colour shade). Default: black.

None

Returns:

Type Description SelPlotResult

A SelPlotResult with the p-values xs, the selection function ys, the confidence bounds ys_lb and ys_ub (NaN without a

SelPlotResult

confidence region) and the axes ax (None if draw is false).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

the model has a truncated selection function or none; ci is unknown; xlim or ylim does not have two values or xlim is outside 0 to 1; prec is an unknown string; or ci='wald' is not possible for the model.

Metafor reference

plot.rma.uni.selmodel

docs.title: regplot
docs.text:
Meta-analytic scatterplot (metafor's regplot.rma) and its points method (points.regplot).

Plots the observed effects against one moderator of a meta-regression model, with the size of each point given by its weight (or a precision), the fitted regression line and, optionally, the pointwise confidence and prediction bands. See https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/regplot.html, https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/regplot.rma.r, https://github.com/wviechtb/metafor/blob/master/R/points.regplot.r and Thompson & Higgins (2002), doi:10.1002/sim.1187.

docs.title: RegplotResult dataclass
docs.text:
RegplotResult(
    ax: Axes,
    xi: FloatArray,
    yi: FloatArray,
    psize: FloatArray,
    pred: FloatArray | None,
    label: NDArray[bool_],
    slab: tuple[str, ...],
    order: NDArray[intp],
    offset: tuple[float, ...],
    labsize: float,
    ids: NDArray[intp],
    pch: tuple[int, ...],
    col: tuple[Any, ...],
    bg: tuple[Any, ...],
)

The plotted points (what metafor's regplot() returns invisibly) and the axes drawn on.

xi and yi are the coordinates of the studies drawn (yi after any transformation), psize the symbol sizes (the cex of the points), label which studies were labelled, pred the fitted values and order the order in which the points were drawn (largest symbols first). ids are the 0-based positions of the studies among the rows supplied, pch, col and bg the symbols and colours of the points, and offset and labsize those of the labels, so that :func:points_regplot can redraw the points and labels (metafor's points() of a regplot object).

docs.title: regplot
docs.text:
regplot(
    x: RMAResult
    | RMAMVResult
    | FixedBinaryResult
    | RMALSResult
    | SelmodelResult
    | GLMMResult,
    mod: str | int | None = None,
    pred: bool | PredictResult = True,
    ci: bool = True,
    pi: bool = False,
    shade: bool | str | Sequence[str] = True,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    predlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    olim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    xlab: str | None = None,
    ylab: str | None = None,
    at: ArrayLike | None = None,
    digits: float | Sequence[float] = 2,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    atransf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    level: float | None = None,
    pch: int | Sequence[int] = 21,
    psize: float | str | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    plim: Sequence[float] = (0.5, 3.0),
    col: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    bg: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    slab: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
    grid: bool | str = False,
    refline: float | None = None,
    label: bool | str | Sequence[Any] = False,
    offset: float | Sequence[float] = (1.0, 1.0),
    labsize: float = 1.0,
    lcol: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    lty: str | int | Sequence[str | int] | None = None,
    legend: bool | str | dict[str, Any] = False,
    xvals: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    bty: str = 'o',
    las: int = 0,
    grep: bool = False,
    fixed: bool = False,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    xaxt: str = 's',
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
    at_lab: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    box_lty: str = 'solid',
) -> RegplotResult

Meta-analytic scatterplot of a meta-regression model (regplot.rma).

Mirrors metafor's regplot().

mod is the moderator on the horizontal axis (its name, or its 0-based position among the coefficients; it may be left out when the model has a single moderator). The regression line (pred) and the confidence (ci) and prediction (pi) bands are drawn for the other moderators set to their means; xvals gives the moderator values to predict at, and pred may be a PredictResult for those values. transf transforms the effects and the bands, atransf only the labels of the vertical axis, and olim limits the values drawn. The points have the cex psize (or the square roots of the weights rescaled to plim; give 'seinv' or 'vinv' to scale the inverse standard errors or variances instead). label labels the studies (True/'all', 'ciout'/'piout' for those outside the bands, a boolean array or 0-based indices), with offset the distance from the point in percent of the vertical range and labsize the text size. legend adds a legend (True, a location such as 'topright' or a dict with x and cex); box_lty is the line type of its frame ('blank' for none). at_lab gives the labels of the ticks at of the vertical axis (one per value of at, or per tick when at is not given) instead of the formatted values.

bty ('o' or 'l') is the box type and las the orientation of the labels of the vertical axis (0 = parallel to it, 1 = horizontal). xaxt='n' leaves out the horizontal axis. grep=True makes a string mod a regular expression searched for in the coefficient names (which must find exactly one) and fixed=True a literal string instead (the grep and fixed arguments metafor reads through ...). na_action stands for R's options(na.action=): 'fail' stops when the regression line is drawn (pred=True) and studies were left out of the fit, the other choices give the same plot.

x is a fit of rma, including location-scale models, of selmodel, of rma_mv or of rma_glmm; the bands are the predictions of the model, so no prediction interval is drawn where predict gives none (location-scale models). The sizes of the points are equal for the models without weights (selmodel and rma_glmm fits).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x RMAResult | RMAMVResult | FixedBinaryResult | RMALSResult | SelmodelResult | GLMMResult

A fitted meta-regression model: rma_uni (including location-scale models), selmodel, rma_mv or rma_glmm.

required mod str | int | None

Moderator on the horizontal axis: its name (matched exactly or as the start of one coefficient name), or its 0-based position among the coefficients (the intercept, if any, is position 0). May be left out when the model has a single moderator.

None pred bool | PredictResult

Draw the regression line (the other moderators are set to their means), or give a PredictResult for the values in xvals. Default: True.

True ci bool

Draw the confidence band. Default: True.

True pi bool

Draw the prediction band (none is drawn, with a warning, where the model gives no prediction interval). Default: False.

False shade bool | str | Sequence[str]

Shade the bands: True (the default, light greys), False, or colour(s) for the confidence and prediction bands (a single colour serves both).

True xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis as (low, high). Default: the range of the moderator.

None ylim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high). Default: the range of the (transformed) estimates and of the prediction band (if drawn) or confidence band, extended to include at.

None predlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits (low, high) of the moderator values for the regression line and bands. Default: the range of the moderator extended by 4 percent on each side.

None olim Sequence[float] | None

Limits (low, high) the estimates and the line and band bounds cannot exceed, for bounded measures. Default: none.

None xlab str | None

Label of the horizontal axis. Default: the coefficient name.

None ylab str | None

Label of the vertical axis. Default: derived from the effect size measure and transf/atransf.

None at ArrayLike | None

Positions of the tick marks of the vertical axis (on the transformed scale of transf, before atransf). Default: chosen automatically.

None digits float | Sequence[float]

Number of decimals of the vertical-axis tick labels (trailing zeros are kept) and of the level in the legend. Default: 2.

2 transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to the estimates and to the line and band bounds before they are drawn. Not together with atransf.

None atransf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to the vertical-axis tick labels only. Not together with transf.

None targs Any

Additional arguments passed to transf or atransf.

None level float | None

Confidence level of the bands (95 or 0.95 for 95 percent). Default: the level of the model.

None pch int | Sequence[int]

Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code), or one per study used in the fit. Default: 21, a circle with border col and fill bg.

21 psize float | str | Sequence[float] | None

Size (expansion factor) of the points: a number, one per study used in the fit, or 'seinv'/'vinv' to make the sizes proportional to the inverse standard errors or variances (rescaled to plim). Default: the square roots of the weights rescaled to plim (equal sizes for models without weights).

None plim Sequence[float]

Range (min, max) of the point sizes when psize is not a number or vector, with an optional third value as the minimum size. NaN for min scales the largest to max (the third value then enforces a minimum size); NaN for max scales the smallest to min (the third value then enforces a maximum size). Default: (0.5, 3).

(0.5, 3.0) col str | Sequence[str] | None

Border colour of the points, or one per study used in the fit (a matplotlib colour). Default: black.

None bg str | Sequence[str] | None

Fill colour of the points for symbols with a separate fill, or one per study used in the fit. Default: grey.

None slab Sequence[Any] | None

Study labels (for label): one per row of the data passed to the model fit, those of studies left out of the fit are dropped. Default: those of the model.

None grid bool | str

Add a grid: True, False or a colour string for the grid lines. Default: False.

False refline float | None

Position of a horizontal reference line. Default: none.

None label bool | str | Sequence[Any]

Label the studies: True or 'all', 'ciout'/'piout' for those outside the confidence/prediction band, a boolean array (one per study used in the fit) or 0-based indices of the studies used in the fit. Labels are above the points above the regression line, otherwise below. Default: False.

False offset float | Sequence[float]

Distance of the labels from the points, in percent of the vertical range: one value (a multiple of the point size) or a pair (added distance, multiple of the point size). Default: (1, 1).

(1.0, 1.0) labsize float

Text size of the labels, as an expansion factor. Default: 1.

1.0 lcol str | Sequence[str] | None

Colours of up to four lines: the regression line, the confidence band bounds, the prediction band bounds and the reference line. A single colour serves all four; two give (line, both bounds) and three leave the reference line at its default. Default: black, black, black and grey.

None lwd float | Sequence[float] | None

Line widths of the same four lines, expanded like lcol. Default: 3, 1, 1 and 2.

None lty str | int | Sequence[str | int] | None

Line types of the same four lines, expanded like lcol. Default: solid, dashed, dotted and solid. Accepts R names ('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash', 'twodash', 'blank'), R codes 0 to 6 or a matplotlib line style.

None legend bool | str | dict[str, Any]

Add a legend: True, a corner such as 'topright' (or a matplotlib legend loc), or a mapping whose 'x' is the location and 'cex' the size (other keys are ignored). Default: False.

False xvals ArrayLike | None

Moderator values to predict at, for the regression line and bands; required with a pred that is a PredictResult. Default: 1000 equally spaced values over predlim.

None bty str

Type of box around the plot, as R's bty: 'o' (the default), 'l', '7', 'c', 'u', ']' or 'n' (none).

'o' las int

Orientation of the vertical-axis tick labels: 0 (the default) parallel to the axis, any other value horizontal.

0 grep bool

Treat a string mod as a regular expression searched for in the coefficient names (must match exactly one). Default: False.

False fixed bool

Treat a string mod as a literal string, not a regular expression (with grep). Default: False.

False ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

None xaxt str

'n' leaves out the horizontal axis; 's' (the default) draws it.

's' na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

What to do with missing values (R's options(na.action=)): 'omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail'; the first three give the same plot, 'fail' raises when the regression line is drawn (pred=True) and studies were left out of the fit.

'omit' at_lab Sequence[str] | None

Labels of the vertical-axis tick marks at (one per value of at or, without at, per tick), instead of the formatted values.

None box_lty str

Line type of the frame of the legend ('blank' for none). Default: 'solid'.

'solid'

Returns:

Type Description RegplotResult

The plotted coordinates and the axes; pass it to points_regplot to redraw the points.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

the model has no moderator; mod is not found or not unique; transf and atransf are both given; psize is an unknown string or label an unknown string; a vector argument has the wrong length; predlim, olim or ylim has the wrong length; xvals is missing with a PredictResult; or na_action='fail' and studies were left out.

NotSupportedError

x is an rma_mh or rma_peto fit.

Metafor reference

regplot

docs.text:

docs.text:
plot_cumul(
    x: CumulResult,
    yaxis: str | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    xlab: str | None = None,
    ylab: str | None = None,
    at: ArrayLike | None = None,
    transf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    atransf: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    targs: Any = None,
    digits: int | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    grid: bool | str = True,
    pch: int = 19,
    cex: float = 1.0,
    lwd: float = 2.0,
    *,
    las: int = 0,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    addgrid: bool | str | None = None,
    na_action: Literal[
        'omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail'
    ] = 'omit',
) -> PlotCumulResult

Plot of the results of a cumulative meta-analysis (plot.cumul.rma).

Mirrors metafor's plot.cumul.rma().

The pooled estimates (horizontal axis) are plotted against the amount of heterogeneity (yaxis 'tau2', 'tau', 'I2' or 'H2'; 'tau2' unless the model is a fixed-effects one), joined in order by a line whose colour runs from the first of cols to the last (light to dark by default). transf transforms the estimates, atransf only the labels of the horizontal axis, digits are the digits of the labels of the two axes and grid draws the dotted grid (a colour for the lines of the grid; addgrid is the old spelling that metafor reads from ... and wins).

na_action stands for R's options(na.action=): an unknown value raises, the others give the same result (metafor sets na.pass while it computes). With 'fail' missing values in the results stop the plot.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x CumulResult

The result of cumul.

required yaxis str | None

Heterogeneity statistic on the vertical axis: 'tau2', 'tau', 'I2' or 'H2' (the first two need a random-effects model). Default: 'tau2' for a random-effects model, 'I2' for an equal-effects one.

None xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis as (low, high), in either order. Default: the range of the (transformed) pooled estimates.

None ylim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high), in either order. Default: the range of the heterogeneity statistic.

None xlab str | None

Label of the horizontal axis. Default: derived from the effect size measure.

None ylab str | None

Label of the vertical axis. Default: derived from yaxis.

None at ArrayLike | None

Positions of the tick marks of the horizontal axis (on the scale after transf, before atransf); the horizontal limits are widened to include them. Default: chosen automatically.

None transf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to the pooled estimates before drawing. Not together with atransf.

None atransf Callable[..., Any] | None

Function applied to the labels of the horizontal axis only. Not together with transf.

None targs Any

Additional arguments passed to transf or atransf.

None digits int | Sequence[int] | None

Number of decimals of the tick labels of the horizontal axis and of the vertical axis: one integer for both or a pair (horizontal, vertical). Default: 2 and 3 for 'tau2'/'tau', 2 and 1 for 'I2'/'H2'.

None cols Sequence[str] | None

Colours (matplotlib colours) of the first and last step; the points and the line change from the first to the last. Only the first and last colour are used (metafor interpolates through all of them). Default: light grey to dark grey.

None grid bool | str

Draw the dotted grid; a colour string sets the colour of its lines. Default: True.

True pch int

Plotting symbol of the points (R's pch code). Default: 19, a filled circle.

19 cex float

Expansion factor of the points. Default: 1.

1.0 lwd float

Width of the line joining the steps. Default: 2.

2.0 las int

Orientation of the vertical-axis tick labels: 0 (the default) parallel to the axis, any other value horizontal.

0 ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

None addgrid bool | str | None

Old spelling of grid (read from ... by metafor); wins over it when given.

None na_action Literal['omit', 'exclude', 'pass', 'fail']

What to do with missing values (R's options(na.action=)): 'omit' (the default), 'exclude', 'pass' or 'fail'; the first three give the same plot (steps with a missing estimate or statistic are left out), 'fail' raises when the results contain missing values.

'omit'

Returns:

Type Description PlotCumulResult

A PlotCumulResult with the axes ax, the plotted (transformed) pooled estimates estim, the heterogeneity statistic yval and the

PlotCumulResult

colour col of each step.

Raises:

Type Description InputError

x is not the result of cumul; yaxis or na_action is unknown, or yaxis needs a random-effects model; transf and atransf are both given; or 'fail' and results are missing.

Metafor reference

plot.cumul.rma

docs.title: llplot
docs.text:
Plot of the likelihood functions of the individual studies (metafor's llplot).

For measure='GEN' each study contributes the normal likelihood of its effect size yi with sampling variance vi; for measure='OR' the likelihood of the (log) odds ratio is the conditional one given the margins of the 2x2 table, which follows Fisher's non-central hypergeometric distribution (Fog 2008, doi:10.1080/03610910701790236). With scale=True every likelihood is rescaled to area one, so that the curves show how much information each study has about the effect. See https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/llplot.html and van Houwelingen et al. (1993), doi:10.1002/sim.4780122405.

docs.title: LlplotResult dataclass
docs.text:
LlplotResult(ax: Axes, xs: FloatArray, lls: FloatArray)

The likelihoods drawn (what metafor's llplot() returns invisibly): lls[i, j] is the likelihood of study i at xs[j].

Values outside of the (very wide) confidence interval of a study are NaN and not drawn.

docs.title: llplot
docs.text:
llplot(
    measure: str = 'GEN',
    yi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    vi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    sei: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    ai: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    bi: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    ci: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    di: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    n1i: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    n2i: ArrayLike | str | None = None,
    data: Any = None,
    subset: ArrayLike | None = None,
    drop00: bool = True,
    xvals: int = 1000,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ylim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    xlab: str | None = None,
    ylab: str | None = None,
    scale: bool = True,
    lty: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] | None = None,
    col: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    level: float = 99.99,
    refline: float | None = 0,
    *,
    onlyo1: bool = False,
    addyi: bool = True,
    addvi: bool = True,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
) -> LlplotResult

Plot the likelihood function of the true effect given the data of each study (llplot).

Mirrors metafor's llplot().

measure is 'GEN' (give yi with vi or sei) or 'OR' (give the counts ai, bi, ci, di, or ai, n1i, ci, n2i). Studies with no cases (or only cases) in both groups (drop00) are left out for 'OR'; if kept, they are drawn dotted, and tables with a single zero count dashed, as in metafor. xvals is the number of points of each curve, level the confidence level of the interval outside which the curves are not drawn, scale rescales each likelihood to area one, and lty, lwd and col are per study (by default the more precise studies get thicker and darker lines). refline draws a vertical line.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default measure str

'GEN' (the default; give yi with vi or sei) or 'OR' (give the counts ai, bi, ci, di, or ai, n1i, ci, n2i).

'GEN' yi ArrayLike | str | None

Observed effect sizes (array or column name of data), for measure='GEN'.

None vi ArrayLike | str | None

Sampling variances (array or column name), for measure='GEN'.

None sei ArrayLike | str | None

Standard errors (array or column name), for measure='GEN'; an alternative to vi, which takes precedence.

None ai ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table counts, upper left cell (array or column name), for measure='OR'.

None bi ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table counts, upper right cell.

None ci ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table counts, lower left cell.

None di ArrayLike | str | None

2x2 table counts, lower right cell.

None n1i ArrayLike | str | None

Size of group 1 (the row total of the first row); an alternative to bi (bi = n1i - ai).

None n2i ArrayLike | str | None

Size of group 2 (the row total of the second row); an alternative to di (di = n2i - ci).

None data Any

Data frame holding the variables named (as column names) in the other arguments.

None subset ArrayLike | None

Which studies to use: a boolean array or an array of 0-based indices (into the data, so lty, lwd and col still have one value per study of the whole data).

None drop00 bool

Drop studies with no cases (or only cases) in both groups (measure='OR'). If False they are kept and drawn dotted. Default: True.

True xvals int

Number of points at which each likelihood is evaluated. Default: 1000.

1000 xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis (the range of the curves) as (low, high), in either order. Default: the range of the confidence intervals of the studies at level.

None ylim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the vertical axis as (low, high), in either order. Default: 0 to the largest likelihood.

None xlab str | None

Label of the horizontal axis. Default: 'Observed Outcome' for 'GEN', 'Log Odds Ratio' for 'OR'.

None ylab str | None

Label of the vertical axis. Default: 'Scaled Likelihood' or, without scale, 'Likelihood'.

None scale bool

Rescale each likelihood so that the area under its curve is (about) 1. Default: True.

True lty str | Sequence[str] | None

Line type of the curves: one value or one per study (of the whole data). Default: solid for 'GEN'; for 'OR' solid, dashed for tables with a single zero count and dotted for those with no cases (or only cases) in both groups. Accepts R names ('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash', 'twodash', 'blank'), R codes 0 to 6 or a matplotlib line style.

None lwd float | Sequence[float] | None

Line width of the curves: one value or one per study. Default: 4 to 0.4, thicker for the more precise studies (by the rank of the sampling variance).

None col str | Sequence[str] | None

Colour of the curves: one value or one per study (a matplotlib colour). Default: shades of grey from dark (the most precise study) to light (the least precise study).

None level float

Confidence level in percent of the interval of each study outside which its curve is not drawn (and which sets the default xlim). Default: 99.99.

99.99 refline float | None

Position of a vertical reference line, or None (or NaN) for none. Default: 0.

0 onlyo1 bool

Passed to escalc: only the first outcome of the 2x2 tables is used.

False addyi bool

Passed to escalc: apply add to the effect size.

True addvi bool

Passed to escalc: apply add to the sampling variance.

True ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to draw into. Default: the current axes.

None

Returns:

Type Description LlplotResult

A LlplotResult with the axes ax, the xs at which the likelihoods were evaluated and the matrix lls of the likelihoods (one row per

LlplotResult

study, NaN outside the confidence interval of the study at level).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

measure is not 'GEN' or 'OR'; the required variables are missing, of different lengths or the counts are invalid; lty, lwd or col has the wrong length; or no study remains.

Metafor reference

llplot

docs.title: plot_permutest
docs.text:
plot_permutest(
    x: PermutestResult | LSPermutestResult,
    beta: Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None = None,
    alpha: Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None = None,
    QM: bool = False,
    QS: bool = False,
    breaks: object = 'Scott',
    freq: bool = False,
    col: str | None = None,
    border: str | None = None,
    col_out: str | None = None,
    col_ref: str | None = None,
    col_density: str | None = None,
    trim: float = 0.0,
    adjust: float = 1.0,
    lwd: float | Sequence[float] = (2, 0, 0, 4),
    legend: bool | str = False,
    *,
    alternative: str | None = None,
    p2defn: str | None = None,
    stat: str | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    layout: object = None,
) -> PlotPermutestResult

Plot the permutation distributions of a permutest result (plot.permutest.rma.uni).

Mirrors metafor's plot.permutest.rma.uni().

One panel is drawn per selected element, in the order of metafor: the omnibus test of the location coefficients (QM=True), the location coefficients, the omnibus test of the scale coefficients (QS=True) and the scale coefficients. Each panel is the histogram of the permuted test statistics (or coefficients), the observed value is a dashed line and the tails beyond it are filled with col_out. The theoretical null distribution and the kernel density estimate are omitted by default (their lwd is 0). A single-coefficient plot has no panel title.

Trimming only affects the histogram; the kernel density estimate uses all permutations.

For an omnibus test with a single degree of freedom (QM=True and one coefficient tested) the theoretical density is infinite at 0. That point is left out of the curve and of the y range, whereas metafor stops with an infinite ylim there.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x PermutestResult | LSPermutestResult

The result of permutest; a location-scale permutation test gives LSPermutestResult.

required beta Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None

Location coefficients to plot, as names or 0-based positions (R: 1-based). A single name or position is allowed. Default None: all coefficients but the intercept (the intercept only when it is the only coefficient). [] selects none.

None alpha Sequence[int | str] | int | str | None

Scale coefficients to plot, selected as beta. Only used for LSPermutestResult; default None: all but the intercept.

None QM bool

Add the panel of the omnibus test of the location coefficients (ignored for an intercept-only model). Default: False.

False QS bool

Add the panel of the omnibus test of the scale coefficients (LSPermutestResult only). Default: False.

False breaks object

The breaks argument of R's hist(): a number of bins, a rule name or a vector of break points. Default: 'Scott'.

'Scott' freq bool

Draw counts instead of densities. Forces lwd[1] and lwd[2] to 0, so no curves are drawn. Default: False.

False col str | None

Fill colour of the histogram bars. Default: '#B3B3B3' (light grey).

None border str | None

Border colour of the bars. Default: '#E5E5E5' (lighter grey).

None col_out str | None

Fill colour of the bars in the tails beyond the observed value. Default: '#FF000080' (semi-transparent red).

None col_ref str | None

Colour of the theoretical null distribution. Default: '#4C4C4C' (dark grey). The dashed line at the observed value and the vertical line at zero are always black.

None col_density str | None

Colour of the kernel density estimate. Default: 'blue'.

None trim float

Fraction of the permutations dropped from the histogram, which must be below 0.5. The omnibus panels drop the upper trim fraction, the coefficient panels drop trim / 2 from each tail. Default: 0.

0.0 adjust float

Bandwidth adjustment of the kernel density estimate, as the adjust argument of R's density(). Default: 1.

1.0 lwd float | Sequence[float]

Line widths of the dashed line at the observed value, of the theoretical null distribution, of the kernel density estimate and of the vertical line at zero (coefficient panels only). A width of 0 leaves the element out. A single number is used for the first three and 4 for the last; two or three values are completed to four (the second is repeated for the third, the last defaults to 4). Default: (2, 0, 0, 4).

(2, 0, 0, 4) legend bool | str

True or a location (for example 'topleft') for a legend naming the curves; drawn in the first panel only and only when a curve is drawn. True places it at the top right. Default: False.

False alternative str | None

'two.sided', 'greater' or 'less'. Default: that of the test.

None p2defn str | None

Definition of the two-sided p-value, 'abs' or 'px2'. Default: that of the test.

None stat str | None

Statistic plotted, 'test' (z or t values) or 'coef' (coefficients). Default: that of the test.

None ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to draw into; the panels are laid out inside it. Default: the current axes.

None xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis of every panel. Default: the range of the histogram breaks. The plotted axis extends 4 percent beyond the limits, as in R.

None layout object

Deprecated and ignored; a warning is issued, as in metafor.

None

Returns:

Type Description PlotPermutestResult

A PlotPermutestResult with the fields axes (the axes of the panels drawn) and names ('QM', 'QS' or the

PlotPermutestResult

coefficient name of each panel, in the same order).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

trim is 0.5 or more; alternative, p2defn or stat is not a valid value; a coefficient name or position in beta or alpha does not exist; no panel is selected.

Metafor reference

plot.permutest.rma.uni

    lwd: float | Sequence[float] = (2, 0),
    *,
    tail: str = 'upper',
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    xlim: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    layout: object = None,
) -> PlotVifResult

Plot the simulated (G)VIFs of a vif result obtained with sim=True (plot.vif.rma).

Mirrors metafor's plot.vif.rma().

One panel is drawn per (G)VIF in x, titled Coefficient: name (Coefficients: name for a set of coefficients). Each panel is the histogram of the (G)VIFs simulated under independence of the moderators, with the observed (G)VIF as a dashed black vertical line and the bars beyond it filled with col_out. A (G)VIF beyond the right edge of the plot is drawn at the edge, with an arrow pointing to it. The kernel density estimate is omitted by default (its lwd is 0).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x VIFResult

The result of vif obtained with sim=True.

required breaks object

The breaks argument of R's hist(): a number of bins, a rule name or a vector of break points. Default: 'Scott'.

'Scott' freq bool

Draw counts instead of densities. This turns off the kernel density estimate. Default: False.

False col str | None

Fill colour of the histogram bars. Default: '#B3B3B3' (light grey).

None border str | None

Border colour of the bars. Default: '#E5E5E5' (lighter grey).

None col_out str | None

Fill colour of the bars beyond the observed (G)VIF. Default: '#FF000080' (semi-transparent red). The observed value itself is always drawn in black.

None col_density str | None

Colour of the kernel density estimate. Default: 'blue'.

None trim float

Fraction (below 0.5) of the largest simulated values dropped from the histogram. Default: 0.

0.0 adjust float

Bandwidth adjustment of the kernel density estimate, as the adjust argument of R's density(). Default: 1.

1.0 lwd float | Sequence[float]

Line widths of the dashed line at the observed (G)VIF and of the kernel density estimate; a width of 0 leaves the element out. A single number is used for both. Default: (2, 0).

(2, 0) tail str

Tail of the simulated distribution filled beyond the observed (G)VIF, 'upper' or 'lower'. Not in metafor, which always fills the upper tail. Default: 'upper'.

'upper' ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to draw into; the panels are laid out inside it. Default: the current axes.

None xlim Sequence[float] | None

Limits of the horizontal axis of every panel. Default: the range of the histogram breaks. The plotted axis extends 4 percent beyond the limits, as in R.

None layout object

Deprecated and ignored; a warning is issued, as in metafor.

None

Returns:

Type Description PlotVifResult

A PlotVifResult with the fields axes (one axes per panel) and names (the coefficient names of the panels).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

x was not obtained with sim=True; trim is 0.5 or more; tail is neither 'lower' nor 'upper'.

docs.title: Transformations
docs.text:
Transformation functions, used as transf= or atransf= in predict, confint and the plot functions. metafor's transf.ilogit is metafopy.transf.ilogit, and transf.ipft.hm is metafopy.transf.ipft_hm. Each is also a top-level function with the mechanical translation of the R name, metafopy.transf_ilogit and metafopy.transf_ipft_hm. Functions with _int and _mode suffixes integrate over or find the mode of the distribution of the true effects, and take targs={'tau2': ...} (some also accept other targs keys, see each function).

Transformation functions (metafor's transf.*).

A port of R/transf.r from metafor 5.2-1. metafor's transf.rtoz is metafopy.transf.rtoz here, transf.ipft.hm is metafopy.transf.ipft_hm, and so on (the remaining . becomes _); the same functions are also metafopy.transf_rtoz, metafopy.transf_ipft_hm, ..., the mechanical translation of the R names. Argument names and defaults are metafor's. The functions are documented on metafor's help page, ?transf (https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/reference/transf.html). Sources cited there:

  • Fisher (1921), r-to-z (Metron, 1, 1-32; the link on metafor's help page, https://hdl.handle.net/2440/15169, no longer resolves);
  • Freeman & Tukey (1950), double arcsine and incidence-rate transformations, doi:10.1214/aoms/1177729756, inverted as in Miller (1978), doi:10.1080/00031305.1978.10479283 (ipft_hm uses the harmonic mean of the sample sizes);
  • Hakstian & Whalen (1976), doi:10.1007/BF02291840, and Bonett (2002), doi:10.3102/10769986027004335, for coefficient alpha;
  • Olkin & Finn (1995), doi:10.1037/0033-2909.118.1.155, for R-squared;
  • Cohen (1988) U1-U3, Inman & Bradley (1989), doi:10.1080/03610928908830127, and Grice & Barrett (2014), doi:10.2466/03.pr0.115c29z4, for overlap; McGraw & Wong (1992), doi:10.1037/0033-2909.111.2.361, for the CLES; Rosenthal & Rubin (1982), doi:10.1037/0022-0663.74.2.166, for the BESD;
  • Jacobs & Viechtbauer (2017), doi:10.1002/jrsm.1218, for (point-)biserial correlations;
  • Cox & Snell (1989) and Chinn (2000), doi:10.1002/1097-0258(20001130)19:22<3127::aid-sim784>3.0.co;2-m, for log odds ratios to SMDs; Pearson (1900), doi:10.1098/rsta.1900.0022, and Digby (1983), doi:10.2307/2531104, for tetrachoric approximations.

Every function accepts array-likes or scalars (NaN or None for R's NA) and returns a float ndarray that is at least 1-d (R has no scalars), with the broadcast shape of the inputs.

The *_int functions integrate with SciPy's QUADPACK qags/qagi, the routines behind R's integrate(), using R's defaults (rel.tol = abs.tol = .Machine$double.eps^0.25, 100 subdivisions); where R's integrate() stops with an error, metafor returns NA and so do these. ilogit_mode uses the line-for-line port of R's uniroot(), exp_mode is a closed form and the other *_mode functions use the port of R's optimize(). exp_int is the closed form exp(xi + tau2/2).

Behaviour kept from R, including its quirks:

  • iarcsin_int, iahw_int and iabt_int bound the integral below by max(0, xi - 10*tau) taken over all xi (and iarcsin_int and iahw_int above by min(pi/2 or 1, xi + 10*tau), also over all xi), so a vector call can differ from elementwise calls, and one NaN in xi makes every value NaN;
  • ztor_mode(NaN) and similar return a number, as R's optimize() replaces non-finite values by the largest double.

Differences from R:

  • with tau2 = 0 the *_mode functions return the plain back-transform elementwise (in R a vector xi then yields every value length(xi) times);
  • targs is a mapping with metafor's list names (tau2, lower, upper, ni, sd) or, as in R, a scalar or a positional vector; ipft_hm also accepts the sample sizes directly (R errors);
  • R's NA and NaN are both NaN.
